SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

Gordon Road Station,
REPORT
Date September 20, 19 32

Subject (in full) Re ejecting of Koreans from Bus Co. premises.

Made by F.S. 138 J. Ball Forwarded by Inspector Hotchkiss

Sir,
Re the above, I beg to report that whilst on at the Bus Co.
on the 14-9-32 at about 4.35 p.m. about 30 Koreans attempted to
enter the Bus Co. compound knowing that only 6 were to be allowed
in, I attempted to stop them from entering, but they resisted
and proved two much for myself and 2 C.P.Cs.
I then immediately sent C.P.C. 2244 to telephone to the
Station for assistance, on the return of the C.P.C. 2244, I and
the 2 C.P.Cs. proceeded to Mr. Shotter's office, I entered Mr.
Shotter's office, just as he was telephoning to Gordon Road Sta-
tion, I asked him did he want to see any of the Korean, he re-
plied yes, allow 6 to enter, and request the remainder to leave
the premises, this I did, but they refused to move and they re-
plied we are not going to leave the premises.
A few minutes later S.I. Firth, P.S. Macauley, one Indian
and 3 C.P.Cs. arrived on the scene. S.I. Firth immediately inter-
viewed Mr. Shotter.
Mr. Shotter stated to S.I. Firth that he wanted them re-
moved S.I. Firth approached them and asked them to leave the
premises, this they refused to do, S.I. Firth then called upon
P.S. Macauley, myself and about 10 C.P.Cs. who had had arrived
in ejecting them when we attempted to eject them, by pushing them
towards the door, they commenced yelling at top of their voices,
and resisted our attempts to move them, S.I. Hancock then arrived
on the scene, and ordered the police to withdraw, and himself
went forward, and remonstrated with the Koreans regarding their
attitude towards the Police. He further told them that Mr. Shotter
the Manager had already ordered them to leave the premises they
had no right there. They still refused to leave and adopted a

戈登路捕房，
报告
日期 1932年9月20日

事由（全称）关于将韩人从公共汽车公司场地驱逐一事。

呈报人 警员 138号 J. Ball 转呈人 霍奇基斯巡官

先生，
关于上述事项，谨报告如下：1932年9月14日下午约4时35分，我在公共汽车公司执勤时，约30名韩人试图进入公共汽车公司大院，明知仅允许6人入内，我试图阻止他们进入，但他们进行抵抗，我和两名华捕难以应付。
我随即派华捕2244号打电话回捕房请求支援。华捕2244号返回后，我与两名华捕前往肖特先生（Mr. Shotter）的办公室。我进入肖特先生办公室时，他正打电话给戈登路捕房。我问他是否要见任何韩人，他回答是的，允许6人进入，并要求其余人离开场地。我照办了，但他们拒绝移动，并回答说我们不会离开场地。
几分钟后，副巡官弗思（S.I. Firth）、巡佐麦考利（P.S. Macauley）、一名印捕和3名华捕到达现场。副巡官弗思立即会见了肖特先生。
肖特先生向副巡官弗思表示希望将他们带走。副巡官弗思走近他们，要求他们离开场地，他们拒绝这样做。副巡官弗思随后叫来巡佐麦考利、我自己以及大约10名已到达的华捕协助驱逐他们。当我们试图通过将他们推向门口来驱逐他们时，他们开始大声喊叫，并抵抗我们的驱赶行动。此时汉考克副巡官（S.I. Hancock）到达现场，命令警察撤退，他自己走上前去，就韩人对警察的态度提出抗议。他还告诉他们，经理肖特先生已命令他们离开场地，他们无权在此逗留。他们仍拒绝离开，并采取了一种

S.I. Hancock then left the premises, withdrawing all the
Police, with the exception of S.I. Firth, P.S. Macauley and myself
who remained inside. Between this time, and the arrival of the
Reserve Unit Squad at about 6.10 p.m. we addressed the Koreans
several times to leave the premises, but they still refused.
On the arrival of the Reserve Unit Squad, about 10 Foreigners
and several Indians entered the premises and came upstairs, to
where the Koreans were gathered. The Indians were withdrawn to
the rear of the passage, and the Koreans were again requested
to leave, they still refused, so the Foreigner present com-
menced to force them towards the door. The Koreans then started
shouting like madmen and started to struggle with the Police
striking at them with their fists, the Police then had to resort
to a certain amount of force to eject them.

汉考克副巡官随后离开场地，撤走了所有警察，只留下副巡官弗思、巡佐麦考利和我在室内。在此期间，直到后备队小队于下午约6时10分到达之前，我们多次要求韩人离开场地，但他们仍然拒绝。
后备队小队到达时，约10名外侨和几名印捕进入场地并上楼，来到韩人聚集的地方。印捕被撤至通道后方，再次要求韩人离开，他们仍拒绝，于是现场的外侨开始强行将他们推向门口。韩人随后像疯子一样大喊大叫，并开始与警察搏斗，用拳头击打警察，警察不得不使用一定的武力将他们驱逐出去。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Gordon Road Station,
REPORT
Date Sept. 20th, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Re ejecting of Koreans from Bus Company premises.

Made by F.S. 69 Stewart Forwarded by Insp. Hawkins

Sir,
With reference to above i beg to state that about 4.50 p.m.
on the 14th September 1932, I accompanied S.I. Hancock, F. S.
Rossington and a party consisting of Chinese recruits from the
Training Depot to the Bus Coy. on our arrival we found 35 Koreans
ex-employees of the Bus Coy. assembled outside Mr. Shotter's
office. S.I. Hancock remonstrated with the above men to leave
the premises they having no legal right there, but they refused
to move, as Mr. Shotter had already ordered them to leave. They
still refused to leave adopting a very defiant attitude. At
5.50 p.m. a call was put through to the Reserve Unit, which
arrived on the scene at 6.12 p.m. I being on night Duty and
in mufti remained in the compound and did not take part in the
ejection. From what I saw they acted like a lot of wild beasts,
shouting and acting as if they were insane.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
F. A. Stewart
F.S. 69.

日期 1932年9月20日。

事由（全称）关于将韩人从公共汽车公司场地驱逐一事。

呈报人 警员 69号 斯图尔特 转呈人 霍金斯巡官

先生，
关于上述事项，谨陈述如下：1932年9月14日下午约4时50分，我陪同汉考克副巡官、警员罗辛顿（F. S. Rossington）以及一队由训练所招募的新华捕前往公共汽车公司。到达时，我们发现35名公共汽车公司前韩籍雇员聚集在肖特先生办公室外。汉考克副巡官劝告上述人员离开场地，指出他们在此没有合法权利，因为肖特先生已命令他们离开，但他们拒绝移动。他们仍拒绝离开，态度十分挑衅。下午5时50分，呼叫了后备队，该队于下午6时12分到达现场。我因值夜班且身着便衣，留在大院内，未参与驱逐行动。据我所见，他们的行为像一群野兽，大喊大叫，举止如同疯癫。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，
F. A. 斯图尔特
警员 69号。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ............
Gordon Road Station,
REPORT
Date September 19 1932.

Subject (in full) Events Prior to and during the ejecting of Koreans from
Bus Company premises.

Made by S.I. Firth Forwarded by Insp. Hotchkiss

Sir,
Re the above, I beg to report that when the telephone message
was received at the station at 4.50 p.m. I immediately proceeded
to the Bus Co. with P.S. Macauley, 1 S.P.C. and 5 C.P.Cs. in the
Station L/Car. I went into Mr. Shotter's office where he was inter-
viewing a delegation of 6 Koreans, and he informed me that the 35
Koreans outside his office refused to leave the premises and he
requested me to eject them. I spoke to the Koreans in the corridor
outside the office and requested them to leave several times but
they refused to do so. I then called F.S. Ball, P.S. MacAuley and
about 10 C.P.Cs. and attempted to put them out. They began shouting
and resisted our attempt to move them. Just then S.I. Hancock
arrived and ordered the police to withdraw, which they did, leaving
S.I. Hancock, F.S. Ball, P.S. MacAuley and myself in the corridor.
S.I. Hancock then pointed out to the Koreans that no good would
result by them refusing to leave peacefully, he repeatedly asked
them to leave but they adopted a very defiant attitude and simply
ignored his repeated requests. This state of affairs continued
until 5.50 p.m. when S.I. Hancock decided to call out the Reserve
Unit. During this time all the Police were in the compound with
exception of F.S. Ball, P.S. MacAuley and myself who remained
upstairs. The Reserve Unit arrived at 6.12 p.m. exactly. I then
went down and showed the way upstairs followed by about 10 foreigners and 4 or 5
Sikhs. When I reached the corridor in which the Koreans were
sitting I again asked them to move, they refused and I then ordered
the Sikhs to the rear, the foreigners including myself then began
to eject them with what force was necessary. Whilst being ejected
the Koreans began shouting like a lot of madmen and resisted until
the last one was pushed onto the stairway.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
S. Firth
Sub-Inspector.

档案号 ............
戈登路捕房，
报告
日期 1932年9月19日。

事由（全称）关于将韩人从公共汽车公司场地驱逐之前及期间的事件。

呈报人 副巡官弗思 转呈人 霍奇基斯巡官

先生，
关于上述事项，谨报告如下：当下午4时50分接到捕房的电话消息时，我立即与巡佐麦考利、1名特别华捕和5名华捕乘坐捕房的轻型汽车前往公共汽车公司。我进入肖特先生的办公室，当时他正在会见一个由6名韩人组成的代表团，他告诉我，他办公室外的35名韩人拒绝离开场地，并请我将他们驱逐。我在办公室外的走廊上与韩人交谈，多次要求他们离开，但他们拒绝这样做。于是我叫来警员鲍尔（F.S. Ball）、巡佐麦考利和约10名华捕，试图将他们赶出去。他们开始大喊大叫，并抵抗我们驱赶他们的尝试。就在那时，汉考克副巡官到达，命令警察撤退，警察遂撤离，留下汉考克副巡官、警员鲍尔、巡佐麦考利和我在走廊里。
汉考克副巡官随后向韩人指出，拒绝和平离开不会有好结果，他反复要求他们离开，但他们采取非常挑衅的态度，完全无视他的反复要求。这种状态一直持续到下午5时50分，汉考克副巡官决定召出后备队。在此期间，除警员鲍尔、巡佐麦考利和我留在楼上外，所有警察均在大院内。后备队于下午6时12分整到达。随后我下楼带路，后面跟着约10名外侨和4或5名锡克教警察。当我到达韩人坐着的走廊时，我再次要求他们移动，他们拒绝，于是我命令锡克教警察退到后方，包括我在内的外侨随后开始使用必要的武力将他们驱逐。在被驱逐过程中，韩人像一群疯子一样大喊大叫，并进行抵抗，直到最后一个人被推上楼梯。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，
S. 弗思
副巡官。

（批：O.Z. Stin
Information

The following is as near as I can remember what happened at
the Japanese Consulate, when I attended to give evidence on
the 16-9-32.

I was ordered into a room when there were two Japanese
Inspectors, of the Japanese Consular Police, one Foreign
Stenographer and one Japanese civilian acting as interpreter,
and J.P.S. 9. I was then told to state what happened at the
Bus Co. on the 14-9-32. which I did. Then the following ques-
tions were put and replies given:-

Q. Where were you standing, when the ex Korean Inspectors
entered the Bus Co. premises?
A. At the entrance, to the Head Offices.
Q. Why did you attempt to stop them?
A. Because I had received orders, only to allow 6 of them
to enter.
Q. Who told you to telephone to the Police Station?
A. No one I ordered C.P.C. 2244 to do so myself. At this
moment, a Korean ex Inspector was called into the room,
and a conversation in Japanese took place between him and
the Police Inspectors, the interpreter then told me that
the Korean had seen me leaving the garage in the Bus Co.
compound.
Q. What were you doing in the garage?
A. I went to see if C.P.C. 2244 had telephoned the Station.
Q. Where did you go after leaving the garage?
A. To Mr. Shotter's Office.

（批注：O.Z. Stin
情报
9月16日
9月2日）

以下是我尽可能回忆起的，当我于1932年9月16日出席作证时在日本领事馆发生的情况。

我被命令进入一个房间，里面有两名日本领事警察的日本巡官、一名外籍速记员和一名担任翻译的日本平民，以及日本警员9号。随后我被要求陈述1932年9月14日在公共汽车公司发生的情况，我照做了。然后提出了以下问题并给予了回答：-

问：当前韩籍巡长进入公共汽车公司场地时，你站在哪里？
答：在总办事处的入口处。
问：你为什么试图阻止他们？
答：因为我接到命令，只允许其中6人进入。
问：谁让你打电话给捕房的？

Statement

A.B. 8/9）

Sir,
At 4.45 p.m. on the 14-9-32 I was called to the Charge
Room by F.S. Rogers who was on office duty, and he informed me that
the Bus Co. were having trouble with Korean ex-Inspectors. Taking
3 or 4 Foreigners with me and 10 or 12 C.P.Cs. I proceeded in a
radio van to the above place. On my arrival there, I was shown to
the administration officers of the Co., proceeding up the stairs to
the 2nd floor, where Mr. Shotter's office is situated. At the top
of the landing of the stairs, I observed about 35 Koreans some of
whom were struggling with the Police, and now and again an angry
exclamation was heard. Ordering them to withdraw (Police), I
located Mr. Shotter, who expressed a request that they be ejected.
I then interviewed the Koreans and informed them of Mr. Shotter's
wishes and asked them to leave the premises, and they in reply
stated that they would like to ask him a few more questions, to
which I agreed to. This kind of talk went on for about an hour.
Finally Mr. Shotter refused to discuss the matter any further
unless they returned their uniforms to the Co., to which they
flatly refused. Mr. Shotter and other members of the Co. present
were becoming inpatient with my delay in ejecting them. S.I. Firth
and about 4 foreigners had on their arrival by gentle force
attempted to move them from the offices, but immediately hands were
laid on them, they commenced to show fight and no doubt would have
overpowered the Police, had they persisted. I had sufficient
strength to eject them provided I had used the C.P.Cs., I was how-
ever reluctant to do this in view of the local situation. Further
conversations took place between Mr. Shotter, the Koreans and
myself, and despite of repeated requests to leave the premises,
they remained adamant. At 5.50 p.m. (That is after having tried

先生，
1932 年 9 月 14 日下午 4:45，值班警官罗杰斯（Rogers）一级警佐将我叫到值班室，他告知我公共汽车公司正与前朝鲜籍督察发生纠纷。我带领 3 或 4 名外侨和 10 或 12 名华捕，乘坐无线电警车前往上述地点。抵达后，我被引见至该公司行政官员处，随后上楼至二楼肖特（Shotter）先生的办公室。在楼梯平台顶部，我观察到大约 35 名朝鲜人，其中一些人正在与警察挣扎，不时听到愤怒的呼喊声。我命令警察撤退，随后找到肖特先生，他表示希望将这些人驱逐出去。接着我会见了朝鲜人，告知他们肖特先生的意愿，并请他们离开该处所，他们回答说想再问他几个问题，我对此表示同意。这样的谈话持续了大约一小时。最后，肖特先生拒绝进一步讨论此事，除非他们归还制服给公司，对此他们断然拒绝。肖特先生及在场的其他公司成员对我迟迟未将他们驱逐感到不耐烦。副巡长弗思（Firth）和大约 4 名外侨抵达后，曾试图以温和的手段将他们从办公室移走，但一旦动手接触，他们便开始反抗，毫无疑问，如果警方坚持这样做，他们本会制服警察。如果我动用华捕，我有足够的力量将他们驱逐，然而鉴于当地局势，我不愿这样做。肖特先生、朝鲜人和我之间进行了进一步的交谈，尽管反复要求他们离开该处所，他们仍态度强硬。下午 5:50（即在尝试

Made by P.S. 363 Macauley. Forwarded by Insp. Hutchison
Sir,
With reference to above I beg to state that about 4.50 p.m.
14th 1932, I accompanied S.I. Firth and a party consisting of 1
Indian and 3 C.P.C.s to the General Omnibus Coy. on Connaught Rd.
where S.I. Firth interviewed the manager, Mr. Shotter;
Mr. Shotter pointed out a party of Koreans numbering 35 to
S.I. Firth and stated that he wished them removed. S.I. Firth
then approached them and asked them to leave the premises. This
they refused to do. S.I. Firth then called P.S. Ball and a party
of 10 C.P.C.s who had arrived to assist as in ejecting them.
When we attempted to eject them by means of pushing them towards
the exit, they commenced yelling at the top of their voices, and
resisting our attempts to move them. S.I. Hancock who had then
arrived on the scene, ordered the Police to withdraw, and himself
went forward and remonstrated with the Koreans regarding their
attitude toward the Police. He further pointed out to them, that
as Mr. Shotter, the manager had already ordered them to leave the
premises they had no legal right there. They still refused to
leave however, and adopted a defiant attitude towards S.I. Hancock.
S.I. Hancock then left the premises withdrawing all the Police
present with the exception of S.I. Firth, P.S. Ball and myself
who remained inside. Between this time, and the arrival of the
Reserve Unit Squad at about 6.10 p.m., we spoke to the Koreans
on several occasions asking them to leave but they continued to
ignore our request. On the arrival of the Reserve Unit Squad,
10 foreigners and several Indians entered the premises and came
up the stairs to where the Koreans were gathered. The Indians
were withdrawn to the rear of the premises and the Koreans were
again asked to leave. They still refused, so the foreigners

先生，
关于上述事宜，谨陈述如下：1932 年 14 日下午约 4:50，我陪同副巡长弗思（Firth）及一支由 1 名印度人和 3 名华捕组成的小队，前往康纳路（Connaught Rd.）的通用公共汽车公司（General Omnibus Coy.），副巡长弗思会见了经理肖特（Shotter）先生；
肖特先生向副巡长弗思指出有一伙共计 35 人的朝鲜人，并表示希望将他们移除。副巡长弗思随即走近他们，要求他们离开该处所。他们拒绝这样做。副巡长弗思随后叫来鲍尔（Ball）警长及一支前来协助驱逐的 10 人华捕小队。
当我们试图通过将他们推向出口的方式来驱逐他们时，他们开始大声喊叫，并抵抗我们移动他们的企图。当时已抵达现场的副巡长汉考克（Hancock）命令警察撤退，他自己走上前去，就朝鲜人对警察的态度提出抗议。他还向他们指出，既然经理肖特先生已命令他们离开该处所，他们在此已无合法权利。然而，他们仍然拒绝离开，并对副巡长汉考克采取挑衅态度。随后，副巡长汉考克离开该处所，撤走了除副巡长弗思、鲍尔警长和我之外所有在场的警察，我们三人留在室内。在此期间，直至后备队小队于大约下午 6:10 抵达，我们多次与朝鲜人交谈，要求他们离开，但他们继续无视我们的请求。后备队小队抵达后，10 名外侨和几名印度人进入该处所，并走上楼梯来到朝鲜人聚集的地方。印度人被撤至该处所的后方，再次要求朝鲜人离开。他们仍然拒绝，于是外侨

I beg to report that the necessary Police witnesses and Mr
Shotter, were assembled at the above Consulate by 10 a.m.
All were then ushered into a very large 2nd floor office, when the
presiding officials, three in number arrived. One wore the rank of
Inspector of Consular Police, a second, the equivalent to our
Sub-Inspector of Police, the third, a Japanese civilian as interpreter.
All of us were then asked to leave the office with the exception
of Mr Shotter, who was under cross-examination until noon. The
Senior Official (Inspector), then informed me that only F.S. Ball
and myself need attend that afternoon. At 2 p.m. the same Court
assembled, with the addition of a Foreign girl as Court writer secured
from some office on Kiangse Road. Sgt Ball was then called and
cross-examined for about 3 hours . I once approached the desk at
which all sat, seeing that Sgt Ball was getting rather perturbed, but
I was ordered out of earshot by the Inspector. At the close of
Sgt Ball's cross-examination (Approximately 5 o'clock ) the
Court decided to remove to the main offices due to darkness, then
I was called to the desk. The examination proceeded roughly as
far as I can remember as follows :-
(Q) You were connected with this incident on the 14th.
(A) Yes.
(Q) Did you take part in the actual beating of the Koreans.
(A) No, I was armed only with a light stick.
(Q) Tell, all that you know of the incident.
(R) At 4.45 p.m. on 14-9-32, I was informed by the Charge Room
Sergeant, that a number of Koreans had entered the Bus Company's

主题（全称）“关于 1932 年 9 月 15 日在日本领事馆诉讼程序的报告。”

由副巡长詹诺克（Jannock）撰写。由哈钦森（Hutchinson）督察转呈。

先生，
谨报告，必要的警方证人及肖特（Shotter）先生已于上午 10 时在上述领事馆集结。随后所有人被引入一间非常大的二楼办公室，此时三位主审官员到达。一人佩戴领事警察督察衔，第二人相当于我方警署副巡长，第三人为一名担任翻译的日本平民。
随后，除肖特先生外，我们所有人被要求离开办公室，肖特先生接受交叉讯问直至中午。高级官员（督察）随后告知我，下午只需鲍尔（Ball）一级警佐和我出席。下午 2 时，同一法庭再次开庭，另增加一名从江西路某办事处雇来的外籍女孩担任法庭书记员。随后传唤鲍尔警长，对其进行了约 3 小时的交叉讯问。我曾一度走近众人就座的桌案，因为看到鲍尔警长变得相当不安，但我被督察责令退至听不见声音的地方。在鲍尔警长交叉讯问结束时（大约 5 点），法庭决定因天色昏暗移至主办公室，随后我被叫到桌案前。据我所忆，讯问大致如下：-
（问）你参与了 14 日的这一事件。
（答）是的。
（问）你是否参与了对朝鲜人的实际殴打。
（答）没有，我只配备了一根轻警棍。
（问）讲述你所知的关于该事件的一切。
（答）1932 年 9 月 14 日下午 4:45，值班室警长告知我，一批朝鲜人进入了公共汽车公司

premises at Connaught Road, and Mr Shotter requested the Police to
eject them. Taking three Foreigners and ten or twelve S.P.C's ,
I proceeded there.

(Q) What did you do when you arrived there.
(A) I interviewed Mr Shotter.

(Q) What was the attitude of the Koreans.
(A) Most of them were sitting down outside Mr Shotters office,
and had adopted a defiant attitude.

(Q) What was the result of your interview with Mr Shotter.
(A) That an agreement could not be arrived at between them,
and fearing mischief he wanted them ejected.

(Q) Were the Koreans making any trouble then.
(A) No, but they were in an angry frame of mind.

(Q) Then did you tell them to go.
(A) Yes, but they stated that they wanted to ask Mr Shotter a
question, but after conversing with Mr Shotter, they still
could not arrive at a settlement, and the latter repeated his
request that I eject them

(Q) Then what happened.
(A) I and the few Foreigners with me, about four or five, by gentle
force tried to remove them, and immediately we laid hands on
them, they showed fight. Seeing my foreign strength
insufficiently strong, I ordered my men to desist and withdrew

康纳路（Connaught Road）的处所，肖特先生（Mr Shotter）请求警方将他们驱逐。我带领三名外籍人员和十至十二名华籍巡捕（S.P.C's）前往该处。

（问）你到达那里后做了什么。
（答）我会见了肖特先生。

（问）朝鲜人的态度如何。
（答）他们大多数人坐在肖特先生办公室外面，表现出挑衅的态度。

（问）你会见肖特先生的结果如何。
（答）双方无法达成协议，他担心发生骚乱，希望将他们驱逐。

（问）当时朝鲜人在制造麻烦吗。
（答）没有，但他们情绪愤怒。

（问）那你叫他们走了吗。
（答）是的，但他们表示想问肖特先生一个问题，但在与肖特先生交谈后，他们仍无法达成和解，后者再次请求我将他们驱逐。

（问）然后发生了什么。
（答）我和随行的几名外籍人员，大约四五人，试图用温和的力量将他们移除，当我们一动手，他们就进行反抗。鉴于我的外籍警力不足，我命令手下停止行动并撤退

(A) Because we have a Reserve Unit for dealing with matters of this

(Q) Why did you call the Reserve Unit.
(A) Because my foreign strength was insufficient to eject them,
the Reserve Unit is commanded by a Superintendent who is a
far senior rank to me, and they are in a position to carry out

(Q) But in large cities, these Special Squads are only called out

他们沿通往办公室的楼梯向下撤退，鉴于他们的态度以及我们人数处于劣势。随后我反复通过劝告要求他们离开该处所。

（问）你为什么不给虹口打电话调派日本巡捕。
（答）因为我们有预备队来处理此类事务。

（问）你为何不通知日本领事馆，他们是日本臣民。
（答）我暂时忘记了这一点，如果我身边有一名日本巡捕，我就会这样做，将来也会这样做。

（问）你为什么调用预备队。
（答）因为我的外籍警力不足以驱逐他们，预备队由一名级别远高于我的警司指挥，他们能够更高效地执行驱逐行动。

（问）但在大城市中，这些特别小队只有在事态非常严重时才会出动。
（答）我认为情况确实如此，事关重大。

（问）这些人中有些受了重伤，是被警棍击打身体所致。
（答）较严重的伤势可能是在逃避逮捕等过程中造成的。

(Q) A man can be killed with a baton.
(A) Not easily on the body, possibly on the head.

(Q) What right have you to eject these people.
(A) On request of the occupier of the premises who, if thinking
his property and personal safety is in danger. That is the
common law of the people of all nations. I have taken part
in the Nagai Wata Kaisha Mills disturbances and ejected
labourers under the same circumstances.
(R) You should not make that statement, there were Communists
and Radicals amongst those labourers, these were peaceful
Japanese subjects.
(A) I am merely quoting duties which the Police are called upon
to perform.
(R) But there is no parallel.

(Q) What happened then, when the Reserve Unit arrived.
(A) I am superceded then by the Superintendent i/c of the Unit.

(Q) Can you remember of any incident which took place, this office
has information that some of the Koreans were kicked whilst
lying on the ground and some were thrown down the stairs.

(A) I most strongly object to that statement who ever made it,
I saw no person kicked, it is not the action of a Police
Officer.

(Q) Where was you at this time.
(A) At the foot of the stairs.

（问）警棍可以打死人。
（答）击打身体部位不容易致死，击打头部则有可能。

（问）你有什么权利驱逐这些人。
（答）应处所占用者的请求，如果他认为其财产和人身安全受到威胁。这是各国人民的普通法。我曾参与永井棉纱厂（Nagai Wata Kaisha Mills）的骚乱，并在相同情况下驱逐过劳工。
（记录员）你不该那样说，那些劳工中有共产党人和激进分子，而这些是和平的日本臣民。
（答）我只是在引用警方被要求履行的职责。
（记录员）但这没有可比性。

（问）那么，当预备队到达时发生了什么。
（答）随后由负责该单位的警司接管指挥权。

（问）你还记得发生的任何事件吗，本办事处掌握的信息显示，一些朝鲜人躺在地上时被踢踹，还有一些人被推下楼梯。

（答）我强烈反对无论谁做出的这一陈述，我没有看到任何人被踢，这不是警官的行为。

（问）当时你在哪里。
（答）在楼梯底部。

(Q) Was not your place at the head of the stairs.
(A) Yes, but I could not get there, it was all over in a few seconds
and the stairs was a struggling mass of people.

(Q) How many people did you see injured.
(A) About twelve were slightly injured.

(Q) Why didn't you send them to Hospital.
(A) None appeared too serious and all were sent to the Consulate
and Hospital with the least possible delay.

(Q) Why did you not have Japanese Policemen with you.
(A) Because those off duty live in outside quarters, the others
are distributed around the district at Villas etc.

(Q) Would you blame the Koreans for this.
(A) They certainly are not blameless.

(Q) In view of the injuries they have recieved .
(A) Yes.

(Q) Here is a Korean with a leg wound, will you have him taken to
Hospital.
(A) Certainly. (This was done)

About six of the Koreans who participated in the trouble, were
brought in front of me and were asked something In Japanese, to
which I think they replied in the affirmative. (Possibly
identification). Proceedings closed at about 8 p.m.

I am, Sir
Your Obedient Servant,
S. Hancock.
Sub-Inspector.

（问）你的位置不是在楼梯顶部吗。
（答）是的，但我无法到达那里，一切在几秒钟内就结束了，楼梯上是一团混战的人群。

（问）你看到多少人受伤。
（答）大约十二人受轻伤。

（问）你为什么不送他们去医院。
（答）看起来都不算太严重，所有人都以尽可能快的速度被送往领事馆和医院。

（问）你为什么没有日本巡捕随行。
（答）因为下班的人住在外部宿舍，其他人则分布在辖区内的别墅等地。

（问）你会因此责怪朝鲜人吗。
（答）他们当然并非毫无责任。

（问）考虑到他们所受的伤势。
（答）是的。

（问）这里有一个腿部受伤的朝鲜人，你会让他去医院吗。
（答）当然。（已照办）

大约六名参与骚乱的朝鲜人被带到我面前，有人用日语问了他们一些问题，我想他们给予了肯定的回答。（可能是指认）。程序于晚上8点左右结束。

阁下，
您忠实的仆人，
S. Hancock.
副督察。

September 18, 1932.

Enquiry at Japanese, Police Court
(Omnibus Co. - Korean Dispute)

Commissioner.

Sir,

I beg to report the results of the Enquiry held at
the Japanese Police Court on Saturday September 17, 1932
and forward herewith a summary of the questions and answers
etc: asked.

I pointed out to the Official in Charge that it would
help him considerably if he allowed me to make a statement
of exactly what took place from the time of my arrival and
that afterwards he could put any question he wished to me.
This he definitely refused to do and stated he would ask
questions.

On several occasions when I quoted extracts from mine
and the other men's reports (copies of which were forwarded
to H/Q 17-9-32) which was the answer to the question asked,
he did not want to record it and waved the reports aside.

Sub/Inspt: Montgomery who was under examination on
Saturday afternoon was informed that I had stated that he was
in charge of the men who entered the Building, whereas the
report I made was as follows:-

Yes, S.I. Montgomery and F.P.S. Vaughan-Ncale. In fact
all the Foreigners who entered the building were in
charge of parties of Sikhs and took their orders from
S.I. Hancock.

The Japanese Official then said this is what Supt: Fairbairn
said:- S/Inspt: Montgomery was in charge - but omitted
to read the remainder, saying you had better tell Supt:
Fairbairn that he is wrong.

At the conclusion of my examination in the morning, during
the absence of the Japanese Officials, the following conversation

在日本警察法庭的调查
（公共汽车公司 - 朝鲜人纠纷）

警务处长。

先生，

谨此报告1932年9月17日星期六在日本警察法庭举行的调查结果，并随函附上所提问题及答案等的摘要。

我向负责官员指出，如果他允许我就从我到达之时起确切发生的情况做出陈述，将对他的工作大有裨益，之后他可以向我提出任何他想问的问题。但他明确拒绝这样做，并表示他将进行提问。

有几次，当我引用我自己和其他人的报告中的摘录（副本已于1932年9月17日送至总部），作为对所提问题的回答时，他不愿记录，并将报告挥到一边。

周六下午接受讯问的副督察蒙哥马利（Montgomery）得知，我曾声称他是负责进入大楼的人员的指挥官，而我所做的报告如下：-

是的，副督察蒙哥马利和外籍巡捕长沃恩-希尔（Vaughan-Ncale）。事实上，所有进入大楼的外籍人员均由锡克人小队指挥，并接受副督察汉考克（Hancock）的命令。

那位日本官员随后说，这就是费尔贝恩警司（Supt: Fairbairn）所说的：- 副督察蒙哥马利负责指挥 - 但省略了其余部分，说道，你最好告诉费尔贝恩警司他错了。

上午我的讯问结束时，在日本官员不在场的情况下，进行了以下对话

page_data.en:
( 2 )

took place between Mr. S. Ikeda the interpreter and myself:-
(1) Mr. Fairbairn I am very sorry for you that this affair
has happened.
(F) There is no reason for you to be sorry for me. This is
a very small case and the Japanese are making a mountain
out of a mole hill.
(I) I have known you for many years and known your friendly
attitude towards the Japanese. This will spoil your good
name, you were in charge of the Riot Squads.
(F) Yes, I am in charge.
(I) Well, I do not want to bring your name up in anything
like this. The Japanese are viewing this matter as very
serious.
(F) This is a very small case, the Japanese forget the number
of occasions the Riot Squads have cleared Japanese Mills
under similar circumstances and in addition to putting
numbers of men into hospital, have Charged the Offenders
in Court and they were sentenced from 11 years imprisonment
downwards. On these occasions the Japanese were full of
praise for the good work done by the Police.
(I) Mr. Fairbairn you do not understand the Japanese consider
this very serious and I wish to let you know their views
on this matter.
(F) If this is serious what about the 150 Chinese Prisoners
that I took over from the Japanese during the trouble?
How many had bayonet wounds all over them and how many of
them died, and they were innocent Coolies.
(I) You do not understand, we must judge each case from how
it arises. The Japanese Consular Police think these
Koreans have been roughly treated. The Japanese Consular
Police asked me to come as Interpreter because you are
concerned in this incident.
On the return of the Japanese Consular Officials this
conversation ceased.

( 2 )

发生在翻译池田先生（Mr. S. Ikeda）和我之间：-
(1) 池田先生：费尔贝恩先生，发生这件事我为你感到非常遗憾。
(费尔贝恩)：你没有理由为我感到遗憾。这是一个非常小的案件，日本人是在小题大做。
(池田)：我认识你多年，知道你对日本的友好态度。这会损害你的好名声，你是防暴队的负责人。
(费尔贝恩)：是的，我是负责人。
(池田)：好吧，我不希望在这样的事情中提及你的名字。日本人视此事为非常严重。
(费尔贝恩)：这是一个非常小的案件，日本人忘记了防暴队在类似情况下清理日本工厂的次数，除了将许多人送进医院外，还将罪犯起诉至法庭，他们被判处的刑期从11年监禁往下不等。在这些场合，日本人对警方所做的出色工作赞不绝口。
(池田)：费尔贝恩先生，你不明白，日本人认为这非常严重，我希望让你知道他们对此事的看法。
(费尔贝恩)：如果这很严重，那么在骚乱期间我从日本人手中接管的150名中国囚犯又怎么说呢？其中有多少人浑身都是刺刀伤，有多少人死了，而他们只是无辜的苦力。
(池田)：你不明白，我们必须根据每个案件的起因来判断。日本领事警察认为这些朝鲜人受到了粗暴对待。日本领事警察请我来担任翻译，因为你与此事件有关。
日本领事官员回来后，这次谈话停止了。

page_data.en:
( 3 )

This conversation clearly shows that the Japanese
have already passed their judgement on this case and that
they are not interested in the Police evidence, apart from
trying to trip them up on minor details, that have no bearing
on the case whatsoever.

W Stairbarn
Superintendent.
page_data.zh:
( 3 )

这次谈话清楚地表明，日本人已经对此案做出了判决，而且除了试图在与此案毫无关系的细微细节上给警方设绊子外，他们对警方的证据并不感兴趣。

W Stairbarn (原文如此，应为Fairbairn)
警司。

page_data.en:
Korean Incident 14th September 1932

Statement made by Superintendent W.E. Fairbairn of the
Shanghai Municipal Police before Inspector Okumura of the
Japanese Consular Police at 10.15 a.m. on the 17th
September 1932.

Interpreted by Mr. S. Ikeda, engaged by the Japanese
Consulate.

Recorded by F.P.S. 337 C.G. Vaughan-Neale, S.M. Police.

Q. What is your name?

A. William Ewart Fairbairn.

Q. My information is that you are in charge of Riot Squads?

A. Yes.

Q. How many Police did you take with you to the Bus Coy?

A. About 46.

Q. What is the combination of the Riot Squads?

A. Three squads consisting of 12 Sikhs and 2 Foreigners 12
Chinese and 2 Foreigners and 12 Chinese and 2 Foreigners.
4 additional Foreigners make up the drivers of the vehicles
and the No. 1 and the No. 2 in charge.
At this point I will say that I did not leave the
Reserve Unit with the Riot squads but arrived on the scene
two minutes after the Squads had arrived at the Bus Company's
Depot.

Q. Does the above number of men include a Sub-Inspector?

A. Yes. There is also a wireless Van in which we always
carry one or two additional Foreigners.

Q. You mean the extra men are drivers of the vehicles?

A. No, not all drivers. The men are always present in the
event of their services being required. I will not say
whether the total number of men was 50 or 52.

Q. When the Riot Squads arrived on the scene what was the
attitude taken by the Koreans?

A. Supt: Fairbairn then demonstrated on paper, the way in
which the Unit "fell in" on their arrival at the Bus Coy,
and stated:- On arrival of the Unit, S.I. Hancock reported
to Inspector Furness that there were 30 to 40 Koreans in
the building, who refused to leave. Inspector Furness
then instructed 8 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs to enter the
building under the charge of S.I. Hancock, whilst he stayed
on the top of the Riot Van and took charge of two Chinese
Squads which remained in the compound.

Note/ There was a lengthy explanation as to how the Unit entered
the building, the cross-examination was then resumed.

Q. Did Inspector Furness enter the building?

A. No.

Q. Did S.I. Hancock make any report to you on your arrival?

A. No, he was inside the building. I saw Inspector Furness.

Q. What kind of report did you receive?

A. Inspector Furness reported that 30 or 40 Koreans were in
page_data.zh:
朝鲜人事件 1932年9月14日

上海公共租界工部局警务处总监 W.E. 费尔贝恩（W.E. Fairbairn）于1932年9月17日上午10时15分向日本领事馆警察 inspector 奥村（Okumura，音译）所作的陈述。

由日本领事馆雇用的池田先生（Mr. S. Ikeda，音译）担任翻译。

记录人：上海公共租界警务处警员 F.P.S. 337 C.G. 沃恩-尼尔（C.G. Vaughan-Neale）。

问：你叫什么名字？

答：威廉·尤尔特·费尔贝恩（William Ewart Fairbairn）。

问：据我所知，你负责防暴队？

答：是的。

问：你带了多少名警察前往公共汽车公司？

答：大约46名。

问：防暴队的组成是怎样的？

答：三个小队，分别由12名锡克教徒和2名外国人、12名华人和2名外国人、以及12名华人和2名外国人组成。另外4名外国人担任车辆驾驶员以及第一和第二负责人。
在此我要说明，我并未随防暴队一同离开后备队，而是在防暴队抵达公共汽车公司车场两分钟后才到达现场。

问：上述人数中是否包括一名副督察？

答：是的。还有一辆无线电车，我们通常会在车内携带一两名额外的外国人。

问：你的意思是这些额外的人员是车辆驾驶员？

答：不，并不全是驾驶员。这些人员随时待命，以备需要其服务之用。我不确定总人数是50人还是52人。

问：当防暴队到达现场时，朝鲜人采取了什么态度？

答：费尔贝恩总监随后在纸上演示了部队抵达公共汽车公司时的“列队”方式，并陈述道：部队抵达时，副督察汉考克（S.I. Hancock）向弗内斯督察（Inspector Furness）报告称，大楼内有30至40名朝鲜人，他们拒绝离开。弗内斯督察随即指示8名外国人和10名锡克教徒在副督察汉考克的带领下进入大楼，而他自己则留在防暴车顶部，指挥留在大院内的两支华人小队。

注/ 关于部队如何进入大楼的问题进行了 lengthy 的解释，随后恢复质询。

问：弗内斯督察进入大楼了吗？

答：没有。

问：当你到达时，副督察汉考克向你作了任何报告吗？

答：没有，他在大楼里面。我见到了弗内斯督察。

问：你收到了什么样的报告？

答：弗内斯督察报告说，有30或40名朝鲜人在

page_data.en:
Page 2

building and that they had refused to leave and had also
threatened Mr. Shotter and threatened to blow up the
gasolene tank. Inspector Furness told me the number of men
he had sent inside the building.

Q. Is that all?

A. No, I was just waiting for you to record my story.
At this point I think it would help you considerably,
if I told my version of the incident and you questioned me
afterwards.

Note. Inspector Okumura stated that he thought it would be
better to put questions.

Supt: Fairbairn stated:- You will make it very difficult
as your questions do not run in the same sequence as my
story.

Inspector Okumura stated that he would continue to put
questions.

Q. Inspector Furness reported that he had sent 8 Foreigners
and 10 Sikhs into the building.

A. Yes.

Q. Did Inspector Furness tell you for what purpose he had
sent these men into the building?

A. Yes, to request the Koreans to leave the premises.

Q. After you received this report from Inspector Furness
did you actually witness the scene of the incident?

A. No, I have already stated that this took place before I
arrived. I was in the Compound and called to Mr. Shotter
to accompany me into the building as it was my intention
to go with him and request the Koreans to leave, but Mr.
Shotter said, "I want them put out, they have threatened
me and threatened to fire the gasolene tank".

Q. In response to Mr. Shotter's request what did you do?

A. I went into the building accompanied by C.S.I. Ku and left
Mr. Shotter standing in the compound. We had proceeded
half way up the staircase, when I saw that all the lights
had been switched off and heard shouting and saw men
fighting with Police at the top of the stairs. I
immediately returned to the compound and ordered the two
Chinese Squads each of which contained twelve men; to
advance at the charge.
I took C.S.I. Ku into the building because I thought
I was dealing with men, who in the event of not
understanding English could understand Chinese, and I
therefore wished to use C.S.I. Ku as an Interpreter.

Q. What happened then?

A. The two Chinese squads were about to proceed upstairs when
the resistance put up by the Koreans was overcome and the
Police were removing the men who were still struggling,
down the stairway.
The Chinese only advanced up one or two stairs and then
returned to the Compound, their services not being
required.
The Koreans were then 'fell in' in the compound and
surrounded by Police. One or two of the men still needed
checking, one caught hold of my arm, I had to smack his
face with my open hand to make him let go.
page_data.zh:
第2页

大楼内，他们拒绝离开，并且还威胁了肖特先生（Mr. Shotter），并威胁要炸毁汽油箱。弗内斯督察告诉了我他派进大楼的人数。

问：就这些吗？

答：不，我只是在等你记录我的陈述。
在此刻，我认为如果我先讲述我对该事件的版本，然后你再向我提问，会对你有很大帮助。

注：奥村督察表示，他认为继续提问更好。

费尔贝恩总监陈述道：这会使情况变得非常困难，因为你的问题与我的叙述顺序不一致。

奥村督察表示他将继续提问。

问：弗内斯督察报告说他已派遣8名外国人和10名锡克教徒进入大楼。

答：是的。

问：弗内斯督察是否告诉你他派遣这些人进入大楼的目的？

答：是的，是为了要求朝鲜人离开该场所。

问：在你从弗内斯督察那里收到这份报告后，你是否亲眼目睹了事件现场？

答：没有，我已经说过，这发生在我到达之前。我在大院内，叫肖特先生陪我进入大楼，因为我打算和他一起去要求朝鲜人离开，但肖特先生说：“我要把他们赶出去，他们威胁了我，还威胁要点燃汽油箱”。

问：作为对肖特先生请求的回应，你做了什么？

答：我在库首席督察（C.S.I. Ku，音译）的陪同下进入大楼，让肖特先生站在大院内。当我们走到楼梯半中间时，我看到所有的灯都关了，听到喊叫声，并看到有人在楼梯顶端与警察打斗。我立即返回大院，命令两支各有十二人的华人小队发起冲锋。
我带库首席督察进入大楼，是因为我认为我在打交道的人如果不懂英语，可能懂中文，因此我希望让库首席督察担任翻译。

问：接下来发生了什么？

答：两支华人小队正准备上楼时，朝鲜人的抵抗被制服，警察正将仍在挣扎的人沿楼梯带下。
华人只向上走了一两级台阶，由于不再需要他们的服务，便返回了大院。
随后朝鲜人在大院内“列队”，并被警察包围。仍有一两人需要控制，其中一人抓住我的手臂，我不得不用张开的手掌打他的脸，让他松手。

page_data.en:
Page 3

Q. How did you dispose of the Koreans?

A. They were sent to Gordon Road Police Station in transport which was provided by the Reserve Unit.

Q. About the fact that the Koreans were reported to you as assuming a threatening attitude, did you see this with your own eyes?

A. No, I was only told by Mr. Shotter that it was so and wished him to accompany me into the building.

Q. When Mr. Shotter told you of the Koreans threatening attitude, did you ask him for any further particulars?

A. Mr. Shotter had told me that the men had threatened him in fact to use his own words he had used the expression "Fix him", and in view of the noise that was coming from the top of the stairs and all the lights having been switched off, I knew that something serious was going on and returned to the compound and ordered the two squads of Chinese to charge, but the Chinese did not get within reach of the Koreans as the trouble had been overcome and the Chinese were ordered to retire.
I think the cheering of the Chinese as they charged had a lot to do with the quelling of the disturbance. It is the usual custom for them to cheer when given an order to charge.

Q. Who told you that the Koreans had switched off the lights?

A. The Foreign staff of the Bus Company told me so.

Q. Do you know the immediate cause of the fighting?

A. The Riot Squads entered the building without drawing their batons. S.I. Hancock then requested the Koreans to leave the premises, to which they refused, as soon as one man was touched by the Police, the rest of them jumped up and commenced to assault my officers.

Q. When did the Police draw their batons? Was it when the Koreans resisted?

A. One of the Koreans who was about to be removed seized hold of the legs of a Policeman and commenced to struggle, at this point the rest of the Koreans jumped up and charged at the Police.

Q. Who gave the order for the Police to draw their batons?

A. If a Police Officer is in danger of injury it is left to the individual man to draw his baton in order to overcome resistance and defend himself against bodily harm.

Q. Did the Chinese draw their batons?

A. Yes, but they did not come in contact with the Koreans.

Q. In spite of the report you received from Inspector Furness that the attitude of the Koreans was that of threatening to kill Mr. Shotter and blow up the gasolene tank. I would mention that when Mr. Shotter and S.I. Hancock came and made statements they did not even mention anything about this now alleged threatening attitude?

A. Mr. Shotter reported it to me.

Q. Mr. Shotter and S.I. Hancock said in their statements that the attitude of the Koreans was quiet and that their only offence was to refuse to leave the premises.
page_data.zh:
第3页

问：你是如何处置这些朝鲜人的？

答：他们被送往戈登路警察局，运输工具由后备队提供。

问：关于有人向你报告朝鲜人采取威胁态度的事实，你亲眼看到了吗？

答：没有，我只是听肖特先生说是这样，并希望他陪我进入大楼。

问：当肖特先生告诉你朝鲜人的威胁态度时，你是否向他询问了更多细节？

答：肖特先生告诉我，那些人确实威胁了他，事实上他用的是“收拾他”（Fix him）这个措辞，鉴于楼梯顶端传来的噪音以及所有灯光都已熄灭，我知道发生了严重的事情，于是返回大院并命令两支华人小队冲锋，但由于骚乱已被平息，华人未能接触到朝鲜人，随后华人小队奉命撤退。
我认为华人在冲锋时的欢呼声对平息骚乱起了很大作用。他们在接到冲锋命令时欢呼是通常的习惯。

问：谁告诉你朝鲜人关掉了灯光？

答：公共汽车公司的外籍职员告诉我的。

问：你知道打架的直接原因吗？

答：防暴队进入大楼时并未拔出警棍。随后副督察汉考克要求朝鲜人离开该场所，他们予以拒绝，当一名男子被警察触碰时，其余的人都跳起来开始袭击我的警员。

问：警察是什么时候拔出警棍的？是在朝鲜人抵抗的时候吗？

答：一名即将被带离的朝鲜人抓住了一名警察的腿并开始挣扎，此时其余的朝鲜人跳起来冲向警察。

问：是谁下令警察拔出警棍的？

答：如果警官面临受伤的危险，则由个人自行决定拔出警棍，以克服抵抗并保护自己免受身体伤害。

问：华人警察拔出警棍了吗？

答：是的，但他们没有与朝鲜人发生接触。

问：尽管你从弗内斯督察那里收到的报告称，朝鲜人的态度是威胁要杀死肖特先生并炸毁汽油箱。我要指出的是，当肖特先生和副督察汉考克前来作陈述时，他们甚至没有提及任何关于这种所谓威胁态度的内容？

答：是肖特先生向我报告的。

问：肖特先生和副督察汉考克在他们的陈述中说，朝鲜人的态度很安静，他们唯一的过错是拒绝离开该场所。

page_data.en:
Page 4

A. I am not responsible for what Mr. Shotter and S.I. Hancock
have said in their statements. I know what Mr. Shotter
told me and have mentioned the fact in my report to the
Commissioner of Police. I will read this paragraph to you:-
"The situation upon my arrival at the Omnibus Company was
roughly as follows :-
(1) The Koreans had refused to obey the Police request to
leave the building, for over an hour.
(2) They had threatened Mr. Shotter.
(3) They had talked about firing the Gasolene Tank.
(4) The building was in darkness (Lights reported to have
been switched off by the Koreans)
(5) They were actually assaulting the Police, who were
trying to peacefully remove them from the building.

Supt: Fairbairn said I now wish to read extracts from a report
submitted to me by Inspector Furness :-
"Mr. Shotter then requested me to have them ejected from the
premises and stated that they had threatened to kill him,
also that he was afraid that they would set fire to over
3,000 gallons of Gasoline which was stored on the premises".

Q. When you received these reports from Mr. Shotter and Inspector
Furness did you see anything which corresponded with their
statements?

A. The fact that when I entered the building, to request the Koreans
to leave and saw them fighting with Police in such a manner
that it warranted my returning to the compound and calling
upon the assistance of two additional squads of Chinese.

Q. Did you receive any reports about the Koreans being in
possession of arms?

A. No, the Police from Gordon Road Station had been on the
premises for about two hours and had there been any suspicion
of the Koreans being armed they would have called our
assistance immediately.

Q. Did you receive any report from Inspector Furness as to why
the Police used batons?

A. No. Inspector Furness remained on top of the Riot Van. I only
received reports from the actual men concerned.

Q. Did you have anyone in charge of the eighteen men who entered
the building?

A. Yes. S.I. Montgomery and F.P.S. Vaughan-Neale, in fact
all the Foreigners who entered the building were in charge of
parties of Sikhs and took their orders from S.I. Hancock.
I have had experience of over 100 Shanghai riots, in this
case the situation was such that the Police entered the
building to request the Koreans to leave, but they all refused
and assaulted the Police, had the Koreans left quietly nothing
of this nature would have happened, but the Koreans thought that
could resist the Police and commenced to assault them. I wish
to read you the last two paragraphs of my report to the
Commissioner of Police :
"It should be noted that the 8 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs who
entered the building with S.I. Hancock did so with their
batons in their pockets etc; and had the Koreans not
page_data.zh:
第4页

答：我不对肖特先生和副督察汉考克在其陈述中所说的话负责。我知道肖特先生告诉了我什么，并且在我给警务处处长的报告中提到了这一事实。我将向你宣读这一段：
“我抵达公共汽车公司时的情况大致如下：
(1) 朝鲜人拒绝服从警察要求离开大楼的请求，持续时间超过一小时。
(2) 他们威胁了肖特先生。
(3) 他们谈论过点燃汽油箱。
(4) 大楼内一片漆黑（据报灯光系由朝鲜人关闭）
(5) 他们正在实际袭击试图和平将他们带出大楼的警察。

费尔贝恩总监说，我现在希望宣读弗内斯督察提交给我的一份报告中的摘录：
“肖特先生随后请求我将他们驱逐出该场所，并声称他们威胁要杀死他，此外他还担心他们会点燃储存在该场所的3000多加仑汽油。”

问：当你从肖特先生和弗内斯督察那里收到这些报告时，你是否看到了与其陈述相符的任何情况？

答：事实是，当我进入大楼要求朝鲜人离开时，看到他们以这样一种方式与警察打斗，以至于我有理由返回大院并呼叫另外两支华人小队的援助。

问：你是否收到过关于朝鲜人持有武器的任何报告？

答：没有，戈登路警察局的警察已经在该场所待了大约两个小时，如果有任何怀疑朝鲜人持有武器的迹象，他们会立即呼叫我们的援助。

问：你是否收到弗内斯督察关于警察为何使用警棍的任何报告？

答：没有。弗内斯督察一直留在防暴车顶部。我只从当事警员那里收到了报告。

问：进入大楼的十八人是否有负责人？

答：有的。副督察蒙哥马利（S.I. Montgomery）和警员 F.P.S. 沃恩-尼尔（Vaughan-Neale），事实上，所有进入大楼的外国人都由锡克教徒小队带领，并接受副督察汉考克的命令。我有处理超过100起上海骚乱的经验，在这种情况下，局势是警察进入大楼要求朝鲜人离开，但他们全都拒绝并袭击了警察，如果朝鲜人安静地离开，就不会发生此类事情，但朝鲜人认为他们可以抵抗警察，并开始袭击他们。我希望向你宣读我致警务处处长的报告的最后两段：
“应当注意，与副督察汉考克一起进入大楼的8名外国人和10名锡克教徒是将警棍放在口袋里等处的；如果朝鲜人没有

page_data.en:
Page 5

assaulted the police they would not have been injured.
The Police only used sufficient force to effectively
deal with the situation.

Q. When you received this Riot Call and hurried your men to the
scene of the incident did you see any signs of a Riot likely
to occur.

A. Inspector Furness will answer that question. I did not arrive
on the scene until 8 minutes after the Unit had reached the
Bus Depot.

Q. According to our information, received from various kinds of
sources, it appears that these Koreans were not out to make
trouble, but only refused to leave the premises until they
had received the money which was due to them.

A. I would point out that the Koreans were on the private property
of a public utility Company who supplied transport for the use
of the community in general. The Company had the right to
call in the assistance of the Police in order that these men
who had sat down in the building for over two hours, might be
ejected.
When I saw these Koreans I realised that it was a case of
having to deal with them firmly and quickly, they were all
worked up and I did not want to take the responsibility of
what might happen nor meet a situation in which the Police
would have been justified to resort to the use of arms.

Q. You say that the Koreans only refused to leave the premises,
in view of their physical strength compared with that of your
Policemen, they could not have stood much chance of resisting
the Police, have you any witnesses who say that they were
attacked?

A. Yes, I will read extracts from F.P.S. Vaughan-Neale's
statement :-

"I received several blows from the men and was finally
kicked in the stomach. I called for assistance, but
owing to about 80 Koreans blocking the passage, men
were prevented from coming to my help"

Supt: Fairbairn added:- There is no place in the world where
a man can kick a policeman in the stomach and not expect to
be struck with a baton, if such an incident occurred in Japan
the culprit would have been struck down with a sword.

Q. Was it not advisable for the Police to use a little more
patience in removing the Koreans?

A. Who said we should use more patience, the Municipal Police
are experienced and capable of judging what action to take.

Q. In view that you had 50 men under your charge, could not these
men have been removed in a more peaceful manner?

A. I want you to understand that these Koreans brought the
assault upon themselves, if they chose to assault the Police
then they must put up with what they get. Had these men
carried out our request and left the building quietly and not
assaulted our officers then they would not have received
their injuries.
In labour troubles it is not the wish of the Police to be
vindictive, but had it been known that these men were going to
make such a fuss, they would have been charged with assaulting
the Police whilst in the execution of their duty, under which
circumstances you would have had no alternative but to
sentence them to seven days imprisonment.
page_data.zh:
第5页

袭击警察，他们就不会受伤。
警方仅使用了足以有效
应对局势的武力。

问：当你接到这次暴乱警报并急忙派遣手下前往
事发地点时，你是否看到任何可能发生暴乱的迹象。

答：弗内斯（Furness）巡官将回答这个问题。我在小队
抵达公交车库8分钟后才到达现场。

问：根据我们从各种渠道获得的信息，这些朝鲜人似乎并非
意在制造麻烦，而只是拒绝离开，直到他们拿到
欠他们的钱为止。

答：我要指出，这些朝鲜人所在的是一家为公众提供
交通服务的公用事业公司的私有财产。该公司有权
请求警方协助，以便将那些在建筑物内静坐了两个多小时的
男子驱逐出去。
当我看到这些朝鲜人时，我意识到必须坚决而迅速地
处理此事，他们情绪都很激动，我不想承担可能发生的后果
的责任，也不想面对一种警方有理由动用武器的局面。

问：你说这些朝鲜人只是拒绝离开 premises（场所/房产），鉴于他们的体力
与你的警察相比，他们不太可能有太多机会抵抗警察，你是否有
证人称他们遭到了攻击？

答：是的，我将宣读外籍警务人员（F.P.S.）沃恩-尼尔（Vaughan-Neale）
陈述中的摘录：—

“我遭到那几名男子的数次殴打，最后腹部被踢。
我呼叫援助，但由于大约80名朝鲜人堵塞了通道，
其他人无法前来帮我”

费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司补充道：— 世界上没有任何地方，
一个人踢了警察的肚子而不指望被警棍击打，如果此类事件发生在日本，
罪犯会被用刀砍倒。

问：警方在驱逐朝鲜人时，是否不应该更有耐心一点？

答：谁说我们应该更有耐心，公共租界警察经验丰富，有能力
判断应采取何种行动。

问：鉴于你手下有50人，难道不能以更和平的方式
将这些男子带走吗？

答：我要让你明白，这些朝鲜人是自找袭击，如果他们选择
袭击警察，那么他们就必须承受后果。如果这些人
执行了我们的要求，安静地离开大楼而没有袭击
我们的警官，那么他们就不会受伤。
在劳资纠纷中，警方并不希望报复，但如果事先知道
这些人会如此大闹，他们就会因在执行公务期间袭击警察
而被指控，在这种情况下，你们除了判处他们
七天监禁外别无选择。

page_data.en:
Page 6

I think you have misunderstood me, I mean could not these
men have been removed without the use of batons?

A. I will read to you extracts from the report submitted by
F.P.S. Smith :-

"They were asked in a civil manner to leave and given
several warnings. When Police started to assist them to
leave they got together and rushed at the Police at the
top of a flight of stairs of which several fell down,
during the scramble the Police were compelled to use
their batons to defend themselves from bodily harm".

Supt: Fairbairn added:- You cannot have men rushing at or
catching hold of Policemen.
I have seen native fights in Korea and if one of those
natives dared to lay his hands on a Japanese Policeman, he
would have drawn his sword and cut him down.
The Koreans in our case are educated men, why did they
not bring their grievance before the Japanese Consul and
thus prevented this incident.

Q. In our opinion it appears that the question itself is rather
simple, now judging from the serious consequences in which
17 Koreans have been seriously injured and in the fact that
8 are now in hospital, what do you think about it? Do you
think it serious?

A. I do not think that it is serious, I will read to you my
view upon the matter, those which I have already conveyed to
my Commissioner:-

"The situation was such that I considered it necessary
to use quick and drastic methods to cope with it. The
fact that a few of them received minor injuries owing to
this, cannot under the circumstances be helped and it is
nothing more than that must be expected to happen to anyone
under like circumstances".

Supt: Fairbairn added:- If anyone assaults the Police they
must expect to get hurt.

Q. Have you any report of any of your men been seriously hurt?

A. No. Policemen are issued with a baton, and it is not part
of their duty to get hurt.

Q. What about F.P.S. Vaughan-Neale who was kicked in the
stomach? Is he alright?

A. Yes, he is here now.

Q. If these people were your Nationals, would you think it
serious?

A. No, I should not.
In 1904 when I was in Nagasaki I witnessed a British
sailor have his arm nearly severed by a Japanese Policeman.
In this case the sailor only pushed the policeman. I have
also seen over 300 men clubed by Japanese.
Do the Consular Police allow themselves to be assaulted?

Inspector Okumura replied:- I am at present only interested
in this particular incident.

Q. Will you inform me when you received this Riot Call and
arrived at the scene, are you authorised to use such drastic
action without first making any enquiries?.

A. I am authorised to use such force as I deem necessary to
restore law and order. As a Police officer you would know
page_data.zh:
第6页

我想你误解了我的意思，我是说，难道不能在不使用
警棍的情况下将这些男子带走吗？

答：我将向你宣读外籍警务人员（F.P.S.）史密斯（Smith）提交的
报告中的摘录：—

“警方以礼貌的方式要求他们离开，并给予了
多次警告。当警察开始协助他们离开时，他们
聚集在一起，冲向楼梯顶部的一名警察，其中几人摔倒，
在混乱中，警察被迫使用警棍以保护自己免受身体伤害”。

费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司补充道：— 你不能让人冲向或
抓住警察。
我在朝鲜见过当地人斗殴，如果其中一个当地人敢对
日本警察动手，日本警察就会拔刀将其砍倒。
本案中的朝鲜人是受过教育的人，他们为什么不向
日本领事馆申诉他们的冤屈，从而避免这一事件的发生呢。

问：在我们看来，这个问题本身似乎相当简单，现在鉴于
17名朝鲜人受重伤的严重后果，以及其中8人目前仍在
医院的事实，你怎么看？你认为这严重吗？

答：我不认为这很严重，我将向你宣读我对这件事的看法，
这些看法我已经传达给了我的总监：—

“局势使我认为有必要采取迅速而严厉的措施来应对。
事实上，其中有几人因此受了轻伤，在这种情况下是
不可避免的，这只是在任何类似情况下任何人都可能
预期会发生的事情”。

费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司补充道：— 如果有人袭击警察，他们
就必须预料到会受伤。

问：你的手下有人受重伤的报告吗？

答：没有。警察配有警棍，受伤并不是他们职责的一部分。

问：那个腹部被踢的外籍警务人员（F.P.S.）沃恩-尼尔（Vaughan-Neale）怎么样？
他没事吧？

答：是的，他现在就在这里。

问：如果这些人是你的国民，你会认为这严重吗？

答：不，我不会。
1904年我在长崎时，曾目睹一名英国水手的手臂差点被
一名日本警察砍断。在那起案件中，水手只是推了警察一下。我还
见过300多人被日本人用棍棒殴打。
领事警察允许自己受到袭击吗？

奥村（Okumura）巡官回答说：— 我目前只关心
这一特定事件。

问：你能否告诉我，当你接到这次暴乱警报并
到达现场时，你是否有权在未进行任何询问之前就
采取如此严厉的行动？

答：我有权使用我认为必要的武力来恢复法律和秩序。作为一名
警官，你应该

page_data.en:
Page 7.

that. Why do you question the authority of the Police.
I have made a study of mob psychology and am quite
capable of using my own discretion. My appointment as
Officer i/c the Riot Squads shows this.

Q. That question was put because the Koreans were on the
premises at the request of the Bus Company.

A. I do not know whether or not they were there at the
request of the Bus Company.
S.I. Hancock was there and was entitled to call our
assistance, if he considered it necessary.
The calling of the Riot Squads does not necessarily mean
there is a riot, we are sometimes called to render
assistance at big fires and processions, etc..
The Koreans dispute with the Bus Company is of no concern
of the Police

====================

I certify that the foregoing is a true copy of the
questions and answers, heard and recorded by me at the
above proceedings.

C. G. Vaughan-Neale
F.P.S. 337.
W S Harbacin Supt

第7页。

知道这一点。你为什么要质疑警方的权威。
我研究过群体心理学，完全有能力运用自己的
裁量权。我被任命为防暴队负责人就证明了这一点。

问：提出这个问题是因为朝鲜人是应巴士公司的要求
留在该场所的。

答：我不知道他们是否是应巴士公司的要求留在那里的。
汉考克（Hancock）副巡官当时在那里，如果他认为有必要，
有权请求我们的协助。
调用防暴队并不一定意味着发生了暴乱，我们有时
被叫去在大型火灾和游行等场合提供协助。
朝鲜人与巴士公司的纠纷与警方无关

page_data.en:
Korean Incident 14th September 1932.

Statement made by Inspector J. Furness of the Shanghai
Municipal Police before Inspector Okumura of the Japanese
Consular Police on the 17th September 1932.

Interpreted by Mr. Ikeda, engaged by the Japanese
Consulate.

Recorded by F.P.S. 81 C.E. Burt, S.M. Police.

Q. What is your name?
A. Jack Furness.
Q. What Station?
A. Reserve Unit, 549 Chemulpo Road.
Q. Is it true that on the night of the 14th of this month
you proceeded to the Bus Company, Connaught Road.
A. That is right.
Q. By whose orders?
A. We received a telephone call from S.I. Hancock reporting
a Riot Call. This is the usual order.
Q. What was the message?
A. Riot Call, Connaught Road, through Central.
Q. Through Central?
A. Yes.
Q. Did you receive this message yourself?
A. No, the Guardroom.
Q. Who was on duty?
A. F.S. Coleman.
Q. To whom did he report?
A. The first thing he does is to ring the alarm, then he
reports to me.
Q. Who was in charge of the Riot squads?
A. I was.
Q. Where was Supt: Fairbairn?
A. He was out on leave.
Q. Short leave?
A. No, to the Carlton Theatre.
Q. What time did you arrive at Connaught Road?
A. 6.14 p.m.
Q. How many Police did you take?
A. 26 Chinese, 10 Sikhs and 8 Foreigners.
page_data.zh:
1932年9月14日朝鲜人事件。

上海公共租界警察 J. 弗内斯（J. Furness）巡官于1932年9月17日
在日本领事警察奥村（Okumura）巡官面前所作的陈述。

由日本领事馆雇用的池田（Ikeda）先生翻译。

由上海公共租界警察外籍警务人员（F.P.S.）81号 C.E. 伯特（Burt）记录。

问：你叫什么名字？
答：杰克·弗内斯（Jack Furness）。
问：哪个分局？
答：预备队，化学路（Chemulpo Road）549号。
问：本月14日晚上你前往康纳路（Connaught Road）的巴士公司，这是真的吗？
答：没错。
问：是谁的命令？
答：我们接到汉考克（Hancock）副巡官的电话，报告有暴乱警报。这是常规命令。
问：消息内容是什么？
答：暴乱警报，康纳路（Connaught Road），通过中央电话交换局。
问：通过中央电话交换局？
答：是的。
问：是你亲自收到这条消息的吗？
答：不，是警卫室收到的。
问：谁在值班？
答：科尔曼（Coleman）警佐。
问：他向谁报告？
答：他做的第一件事是拉响警报，然后向我报告。
问：谁负责防暴队？
答：是我。
问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司在哪里？
答：他外出休假了。
问：短假？
答：不，去卡尔顿剧院（Carlton Theatre）了。
问：你什么时候到达康纳路（Connaught Road）？
答：下午6点14分。
问：你带了多少警察？
答：26名华捕，10名印捕（锡克人）和8名西捕（外国人）。

page_data.en:
Page 2.

Q. Including yourself?
A. No.

Q. How many Vans?
A. 1 Big Van and 1 Radio Van?

Q. What action did you take on arrival at Constance Road?
A. S.I. Hancock told me that there were 6 or 40 persons
inside the building, who refused to leave, he asked me to try
to get them out, he said he had tried several times
to get them out but failed.
Mr. Shotton the manager of the Gas Company also came
and requested that we should turn them out of the building.

Qr. Mr. Shotton came out of an office?
A. Yes, he said that they were threatening to set
fire to 3,000 gallons of gasoline.

Q. What action did you take?
A. 10 Sikhs and 8 Foreigners went with S.I. Hancock and put
them out, using as little force as possible.

Q. What about the Chinese?
A. They stayed with me.

Q. The Van was in the yard?
A. Yes.

Q. And then? please continue.
A. They went inside and Supt: Fairbairn arrived and took charge.

Q. After S.I. Hancock, 8 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs had gone inside?
A. Yes.

Q. What did Supt: Fairbairn do?
A. He went to go inside and then a big shout went up from
inside and he came out and called for the two Chinese
Squads to charge.

Q. What order did you give to the Chinese squads?
A. I gave no order, Supt: Fairbairn called to the Chinese
Squads to charge.

Q. As soon as Supt: Fairbairn arrived, did he enter the
building?
A. No, he talked with me.

Q. Then did he enter or stand in the porch of the building?
A. I think so, I am not sure, the light was not so good.

Q. As soon as you arrived did you order the Chinese out
like this, in accordance with this plan?
A. Yes, I pressed the siren in the usual way. I was on top
of the van.

Q. Then S.I. Hancock took the Sikhs away?
A. Yes, I put him in charge of the Sikhs and Foreigners.
page_data.zh:
第2页。

问：包括你自己吗？
答：不包括。

问：多少辆警车？
答：1辆大型面包车和1辆无线电车？

问：到达康斯坦斯路（Constance Road）[注：此处原文与前文康纳路不一致，照实译出]后你采取了什么行动？
答：汉考克（Hancock）副巡官告诉我，大楼内有6到40人，拒绝离开，他让我试着把他们弄出来，他说他已经试了几次
想把他们弄出来但失败了。
煤气公司经理肖顿（Shotton）先生也来了，请求我们将他们赶出大楼。

问：肖顿（Shotton）先生是从办公室出来的吗？
答：是的，他说他们威胁要点燃3,000加仑的汽油。

问：你采取了什么行动？
答：10名印捕（锡克人）和8名西捕（外国人）随汉考克（Hancock）副巡官进入，尽可能少用武力将他们赶出。

问：华捕呢？
答：他们和我待在一起。

问：警车在院子里吗？
答：是的。

问：然后呢？请继续。
答：他们进去了，随后费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司到达并接管指挥。

问：在汉考克（Hancock）副巡官、8名西捕和10名印捕进去之后？
答：是的。

问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司做了什么？
答：他正要进去，这时里面传出一阵大喊，他退出来，命令两支华捕队冲锋。

问：你给华捕队下了什么命令？
答：我没有下命令，是费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司叫华捕队冲锋的。

问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司一到，就进入大楼了吗？
答：没有，他和我谈了话。

问：然后他是进去了还是站在大楼的门廊里？
答：我想是这样，我不确定，光线不太好。

问：你一到达就按照这个计划下令让华捕出动了吗？
答：是的，我按常规方式按响了警报器。我当时在警车顶上。

问：然后汉考克（Hancock）副巡官带走了印捕？
答：是的，我让他负责印捕和西捕。

page_data.en:
Page 3.

Q. Where was Supt: Fairbairn?
A. He went up to the entrance and I think went inside.
Q. Did Supt: Fairbairn enter this way?
A. I think by the front door.
Q. Where did he give orders to Chinese?
A. I am not sure.
Q. What did you report to Supt: Fairbairn?
A. I told him that S.I. Hancock had taken the Koreans and Sikhs inside to eject some persons who had refused to leave.
Q. What else did you report to Supt: Fairbairn?
A. I told him what Mr Shotter had told to me.
Q. What statement did you make to Supt: Fairbairn re Mr Shotter's report to you?
A. I told him that Mr Shotter had reported that the Koreans had threatened to kill him and set fire to 3,000 gallons of gasoline, also that they had been on the premises for two hours and refused to leave.
Q. How long later did Supt: Fairbairn arrive?
A. About two minutes after my arrival at the Bus Depot.
Q. When you arrived did you know where the Koreans were?
A. No, S.I. Hancock told me.
Q. Where were you at the time?
A. Standing on the top of the Red lorry.
Q. Could you see the 1st floor corridor?
A. No, I could not, nor could I see the Koreans.
Q. Owing to the darkness?
A. No, it was brick wall and I cannot see through that.
Q. What order did Supt: Fairbairn give to the Chinese?
A. Charge, that is an order for the Chinese to advance on the run.
Q. Before he ordered charge, did you hear any sound from inside the building?
A. Yes I heard shouting.
Q. At the order charge, what did the Chinese do?
A. Ran forward to the door, where Supt: Fairbairn was standing.
Q. And then?
A. I do not know whether they went inside.
Q. Did anyone come out?
A. I could not see.
page_data.zh:
第3页。

问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司在哪里？
答：他走到入口处，我想是进去了。
问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司是从这条路进去的吗？
答：我想是从前门。
问：他在哪里给华捕下命令？
答：我不确定。
问：你向费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司报告了什么？
答：我告诉他，汉考克（Hancock）副巡官带着朝鲜人和印捕进去，是为了驱逐一些拒绝离开的人。
问：你还向费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司报告了什么？
答：我告诉了他肖顿（Shotter）[注：原文拼写变化]先生告诉我的话。
问：关于肖顿（Shotter）先生向你报告的情况，你对费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司作了什么陈述？
答：我告诉他，肖顿（Shotter）先生报告说，朝鲜人威胁要杀死他并点燃3,000加仑的汽油，还说他们已经在该场所待了两个小时并拒绝离开。
问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司过了多久才到达？
答：在我到达公交车库后大约两分钟。
问：你到达时知道朝鲜人在哪里吗？
答：不知道，是汉考克（Hancock）副巡官告诉我的。
问：当时你在哪里？
答：站在那辆红色卡车的顶部。
问：你能看到一楼的走廊吗？
答：不，我看不到，我也看不到朝鲜人。
问：是因为黑暗吗？
答：不，那是砖墙，我无法透过它看到。
问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司给华捕下了什么命令？
答：冲锋，即命令华捕跑步前进。
问：在他下令冲锋之前，你听到大楼里有声音吗？
答：是的，我听到了喊叫声。
问：听到冲锋命令后，华捕做了什么？
答：跑向门口，费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司正站在那里。
问：然后呢？
答：我不知道他们是否进去了。
问：有人出来吗？
答：我看不到。

page_data.en:
Page 4.

Q. You arrived at 6.14 p.m. and this arrived as soon
as you arrived?

A. Within a few minutes, I could not see what happened at the
door, as I also had to watch Conductors who were standing
in the yard and see that they did not cause any trouble.

Q. Did you see the Chinese enter the building?

A. No, I did not see.

Q. 150 Conductors in the Compound, you had to watch them?

AA. Yes, I was telling them to be behind the fence.

Q. You paid attention to them and could not see what was
happening in the building?

A. I watched the lot, it was all over in about one minute.

Q. Then what happened?

A. As far as I know, the Koreans came down followed by Police
and were arrested and taken to Gordon Road Police Station.

Q. Arrested by the Chinese in the compound?

A. They were surrounded first and then arrested.

Q. When Supt: Fairbairn first came, did he ask for Mr Shotter?

A. No, he did not ask.

Q. Did you see Supt: Fairbairn look for Mr Shotter?

A. No, he went forward and Mr Shotter, I think was with
S.I. Hancock.

Q. Before Supt: Fairbairn gave the Chinese an order to
Charge did he see Mr Shotter?

A. I do not know.

X Q. When Supt: Fairbairn arrived, he went to the building and
ordered the Chinese to charge?

A. He went forward and may have spoken to Mr Shotter on the way.

Q. How many yards was the van from the building?

A. About 35 yards.

Q. Was it as long as this room?

A. Longer, about twice as long again.

Q. As soon as you arrived, S.I. Hancock took charge of the
Foreigners and Sikhs? There is no mistake?

A. No. S.I. Hancock was in charge.

X Q. According to previous investigations, S.I. Montgomery
took charge.

A. He is in the Riot Squad and entered together with S.I. Hancock.

Q. S.I. Hancock mentions in his statement that after the
Reserve Unit arrived, he was not in charge and is
exonerated from all responsibility?

A. He went with the others, I am not sure whether he went inside.
page_data.zh:
第4页。

问：你于下午6点14分抵达，而此事是在你抵达时随即发生的吗？

答：在几分钟内。我看不到门口发生了什么，因为我还必须监视站在院子里的售票员，确保他们没有制造任何麻烦。

问：你看到那些中国人进入大楼了吗？

答：不，我没看见。

问：大院里有150名售票员，你必须监视他们？

答：是的，我当时正叫他们退到围栏后面去。

问：你留意着他们，因而无法看到大楼里正在发生的事情？

答：我注视着那群人，整个过程大约在一分钟内就结束了。

问：随后发生了什么？

答：据我所知，朝鲜人下楼，警察紧随其后，他们被逮捕并带往戈登路巡捕房。

问：是被大院里的中国人逮捕的吗？

答：他们先是被包围，然后被捕。

问：费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）警司初到时，他询问肖特（Shotter）先生了吗？

答：不，他没有问。

问：你看到费尔贝恩警司寻找肖特先生了吗？

答：没有，他走上前去，而肖特先生，我想是和汉考克（Hancock）副督察在一起。

问：在费尔贝恩警司向中国人下达冲锋命令之前，他见到肖特先生了吗？

答：我不知道。

问：当费尔贝恩警司抵达时，他走向大楼并命令中国人冲锋？

答：他走上前去，可能在路上与肖特先生说过话。

问：厢式货车距离大楼有多少码？

答：大约35码。

问：有这间房间那么长吗？

答：更长，大约是其两倍长。

问：你一抵达，汉考克副督察就接管了外籍警员和锡克教警员？没错吧？

答：没错。由汉考克副督察负责指挥。

问：根据之前的调查，蒙哥马利（Montgomery）副督察负责指挥。

答：他在防暴队中，是与汉考克副督察一同进入的。

问：汉考克副督察在其陈述中提到，预备队抵达后，他不再负责指挥，并被免除所有责任？

答：他随其他人一起行动，我不确定他是否进入了内部。

page_data.en:
Page 5.

Q. When you arrived all police came out, and S.I. Hancock
asked for the Foreigners and Sikhs to go and get the
Koreans out?

A. No, all the police came out of the Van in the usual manner
and I gave S.I. Hancock the Foreigners and Sikhs to go and
request the Koreans to leave the premises.

Q. Did you see S.I. Hancock enter the building?

A. No, but the rest were sent to stay with him.

Q. What about S.I. Montgomery, was he one of the Foreigners?

A. Yes.

Q. What was your duty, did you have to stay on top of the van?

A. Yes, whatever happened.

Q. In this case, if S.I. Hancock had not asked you to take
police inside, who was in charge of the police if you had
to stay on top of the van?

A. S.I. Hancock.

Q. But if he had not been there?

A. There would not have been a riot.

Q. Then he must be responsible?

A. For what?

Q. For what happened inside the building.

A. He went with them.

Q. 10 Sikhs and 6 Foreigners were instructed by you to go inside.

A. Yes and for S.I. Hancock to go with them.

Q. Supposing S.I. Hancock had been a Sergeant, then what
would have happened?

A. The man in charge of the Station must be on the scene. In
this case S.I. Hancock was in charge of the Station.

Q. Supt: Fairbairn came this morning and according to his s
statement S.I. Montgomery was in charge of the party inside.

A. Yes, he was a Sub-Inspector of the Riot squads.

Q. But if S.I. Montgomery was in charge what about S.I. Hancock?

A. S.I. Hancock is senior to S.I. Montgomery and so in that
case he would be in charge.

Q. In case of a riot is a policeman allowed to use his baton
without orders from the officer in charge?

A. Sure, the order charge means the use of a baton.

Q. In this case who gave the order for the use of batons?

A. I do not know I was on top of the van.

Q. When you arrived on the scene did you see anything that
looked like a riot?

A. No, the Koreans were in the building, there was nothing in
the compound.
page_data.zh:
第5页。

问：当你抵达时，所有警察都出来了，汉考克副督察要求外籍警员和锡克教警员去把朝鲜人带出来？

答：不，所有警察都以常规方式从厢式货车中出来，我将外籍警员和锡克教警员交给汉考克副督察，让他们去要求朝鲜人离开该处所。

问：你看到汉考克副督察进入大楼了吗？

答：没有，但其余人员被派去与他待在一起。

问：蒙哥马利副督察呢，他是外籍警员之一吗？

答：是的。

问：你的职责是什么，你必须待在货车顶上吗？

答：是的，无论发生什么情况。

问：在这种情况下，如果汉考克副督察没有要求你派遣警察进入内部，而你又必须待在货车顶上，那么谁负责指挥警察？

答：汉考克副督察。

问：但如果他不在那里呢？

答：那就不会发生骚乱。

问：那么他必须对此负责？

答：对什么负责？

问：对大楼内部发生的事情负责。

答：他随他们一起进去了。

问：你指示10名锡克教警员和6名外籍警员进入内部。

答：是的，并且让汉考克副督察与他们同去。

问：假设汉考克副督察只是一名警长，那么会发生什么？

答：负责该巡捕房的人员必须在现场。在这种情况下，汉考克副督察负责该巡捕房。

问：费尔贝恩警司今早到来，根据他的陈述，蒙哥马利副督察负责指挥内部的小队。

答：是的，他是防暴队的副督察。

问：但如果由蒙哥马利副督察负责指挥，那汉考克副督察呢？

答：汉考克副督察的资历高于蒙哥马利副督察，因此在那种情况下应由他负责指挥。

问：在骚乱情况下，警察是否允许在没有负责警官命令的情况下使用警棍？

答：当然，冲锋命令即意味着使用警棍。

问：在这种情况下，是谁下达了使用警棍的命令？

答：我不知道，我当时在货车顶上。

问：当你抵达现场时，你看到任何看起来像骚乱的迹象了吗？

答：没有，朝鲜人在大楼里，大院里什么都没有。

page_data.en:
Page 6.

Q. When the Koreans came out, did you think that there had
been a riot?

A. Yes, sure, there was a riot, we could hear them shouting.

Q. The Consular Police think that there was not a riot. There
were 31 Koreans, none of them armed and the shouting was
nothing.

A. That is what they think, I think there was a riot in the
building.

I certify that the foregoing is a true copy of the
questions and answers, heard and recorded by me at
the above proceedings.

S. C. Barratt
F.I.S.Cl.

W.H.
page_data.zh:
第6页。

问：当朝鲜人出来时，你认为发生了骚乱吗？

答：是的，当然，发生了骚乱，我们可以听到他们在喊叫。

问：领事警察认为没有发生骚乱。共有31名朝鲜人，均未携带武器，喊叫声也没什么大不了的。

答：那是他们的看法，我认为大楼内发生了骚乱。

兹证明上述内容为我在上述程序中听取并记录的问题与答案的真实副本。

S. C. Barratt
F.I.S.Cl.

W.H.

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit, Eastern Depot.
September 16, 1932.

Riot Call. Omnibus Co. Depot 14.9.32.

Commissioner.

Sir,

Further to the report on the Reserve Unit Morning
State of September 15, 1932 (Copy attached):-

I arrived at the Omnibus Depot Connaught Rd: about
two minutes after the arrival of the Riot Squads and was
informed of the situation by Inspt: Furness. He also
informed me that there were number of Foreigners and
Sikhs in the Building.

I asked Mr. Shutter to accompany me into the Building
where it was my intention to order the Koreans to leave.

Mr. Shutter said "Put them out" and something about
the Koreans having threatened him. I then entered the
building with Sub/Inspt: Ku.

When half way up the stairs, (which was in darkness)
there were sounds of a free-for-all fight taking place on
the first floor. I immediately gave orders to the two
Chinese Squads to advance at the "Charge" and the building
was quickly cleared.

The Koreans were paraded in the Compound and informed
that they would be released two at a time providing they
went away quietly. Several of them were still in a fighting
mood and had to be restrained.

At that time Mr. Shooter came forward and said that
he was afraid that if the men were released that they would
create a disturbance outside on the roadway. I pointed out
that the Police were on private property and that we had no
charge against the men, and if the men did not disperse
when released the Police would quickly deal with them. Mr.
Shutter stated "I want the men charged and will prefer a
charge against them."
page_data.zh:
预备队，东部车场。
1932年9月16日。

骚乱呼叫。公共汽车公司车场 1932年9月14日。

致警务处长。

阁下：

继1932年9月15日预备队晨间状态报告之后（附副本）：——

我在防暴队抵达约两分钟后到达康纳路（Connaught Rd.）的公共汽车车场，并由弗内斯（Furness）督察向我通报了情况。他还告知我，大楼内有多名外籍警员和锡克教警员。

我请舒特（Shutter）先生陪我进入大楼，我打算在那里命令朝鲜人离开。

舒特先生说“把他们赶出去”，并提到朝鲜人曾威胁他。随后我与库（Ku）副督察一同进入大楼。

当走到楼梯半腰时（那里一片漆黑），听到一楼传来混战的声音。我立即命令两支华捕队“冲锋”推进，大楼很快被清空。

朝鲜人在大院里列队，并被告知，只要他们安静离开，将每次释放两人。其中几人仍有斗殴情绪，不得不加以约束。

当时，舒特先生走上前来说，他担心如果释放这些人，他们会在外面的道路上制造骚乱。我指出，警察身处私有财产范围内，且我们并未指控这些人，如果这些人获释后不散去，警察将迅速处置他们。舒特先生表示：“我要控告这些人，并将对他们提出指控。”

page_data.en:
( 2 )

The men were then handed over to Sub/Inspt: Hancock,
i/c Gordon Road District and an escort provided to take
them to Gordon Road Station.

The situation upon my arrival at the Omnibus Company
Depot was roughly as follows:-

(1) The Koreans had refused to obey the Police request
to leave the building, for over an hour.
(2) They had threatened Mr. Shotter.
(3) They had talked about firing the Gasoline Tank.
(4) The building was in darkness (Light reported to have
been switched off by the Koreans).
(5) They were actually assaulting the Police, who were
trying to peacefully remove them from the Building.

The Situation was such that I considered it necessary
to use quick and drastic methods to cope with it. The fact
that a few of them received minor injuries owing to this,
cannot under the circumstances be helped and it nothing more
than that must be expected to happen to anyone under like
circumstances.

It should be noted that the 8 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs
who entered the building with Sub/Inspt: Hancock, did so
with their Batons in their pockets etc: and had the Koreans
not assaulted the police they would not have been injured.

The Police only used sufficient force to effectively
deal with the situation.

W Starbaum
Superintendent.
page_data.zh:
( 2 )

随后，这些人被移交给负责戈登路区的汉考克副督察，并安排护卫将他们送往戈登路巡捕房。

我抵达公共汽车公司车场时的情况大致如下：——

(1) 朝鲜人拒绝服从警察要求其离开大楼的请求，持续时间超过一小时。
(2) 他们威胁了肖特（Shotter）先生。
(3) 他们扬言要点燃汽油罐。
(4) 大楼内一片漆黑（据报灯光被朝鲜人关闭）。
(5) 他们实际上正在袭击试图和平将他们移出大楼的警察。

鉴于局势如此，我认为有必要采取迅速且严厉的措施来应对。事实上，因此导致其中少数人受轻伤，在这种情况下是不可避免的，而且在类似情况下，任何人遭遇此类事情都是意料之中的。

需要注意的是，随汉考克副督察进入大楼的8名外籍警员和10名锡克教警员，是将警棍放在口袋等处的，如果朝鲜人没有袭击警察，他们就不会受伤。

警察仅使用了足以有效处理局势的必要武力。

W Starbaum
警司。

page_data.en:
Form No. 2
G. 25,000-1-32

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ............
Reserve Unit ....... Station,
REPORT
Date September 16, 1932

Subject (in full) Disturbance at the China General Omnibus Company's Depot
Connaught Road on September 14, 1932.
Made by Sub-Inspector J. Montgomery Forwarded by W. Fairbairn Supt.

Sir,
I beg to report that on September 14, 1932 in response to a
Riot Call, I accompanied the Riot Squad, Inspector Furness in
charge, to the above mentioned premises, arriving there at 6.14 p.m.
In the compound of the Depot there were a number of Police
officers amongst which was Sub-Inspector Hancock. The latter
informed Inspector Furness that about 35 Korean ex-employees had
taken up positions in the Company's offices and refused to leave
the premises when requested to do so by the Management and the
Police, and that assistance was required in evicting them.
Eight Foreigners and ten Sikhs of the Riot Squad were ordered
to accompany Sub-Inspector Hancock to the offices to deal with
the Koreans. I accompanied the Police party to the first floor
of the Company's offices and in a narrow passage at the head of
the stairs perceived a number of Koreans sitting on the floor.
I heard someone advise them to leave the premises, this was
followed by the sound of a struggle, but as the light was bad,
I could not see who was actually engaged.
I then took hold of the arm of one of the Koreans who was
sitting on the floor and endeavoured to get him to his feet, at
the same time telling him to get out. The Korean said "No-No",
and shouted something in a language I did not understand. Four
or five Koreans then crowded round me and tried to get hold of
my arms and I was therefore compelled to use my baton.
I saw that other Police officers were placed in a similar
position to myself but I could not see who the individuals were.
In a few minutes the Koreans were subdued and were put out
of the offices into the compound where Supt. Fairbairn took charge.
I am Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. Montgomery
Sub-Inspector.
page_data.zh:
表格编号 2
G. 25,000-1-32

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案编号 ............
预备队 ....... 巡捕房，
报告
日期 1932年9月16日

主题（全称） 1932年9月14日康纳路中华公共汽车公司车场的骚乱事件。
由副督察 J. Montgomery 撰写，由警司 W. Fairbairn 转呈。

阁下：
谨此报告，1932年9月14日，响应骚乱呼叫，我随同由弗内斯督察负责的防暴队前往上述处所，于下午6点14分抵达。在车场的大院内有多名警务人员，其中包括汉考克副督察。后者告知弗内斯督察，约有35名朝鲜籍前雇员占据了公司办公室，并在管理层和警察要求他们离开时拒绝离开该处所，需要协助将其驱逐。防暴队的八名外籍警员和十名锡克教警员奉命陪同汉考克副督察前往办公室处理朝鲜人。我随同警察小队来到公司办公室的一楼，在楼梯顶端的狭窄通道处，看到几名朝鲜人坐在地板上。我听到有人劝告他们离开该处所，随后传来搏斗声，但由于光线昏暗，我看不清实际参与搏斗的是谁。
随后，我抓住一名坐在地上的朝鲜人的手臂，试图让他站起来，同时叫他出去。该朝鲜人说“不-不”，并用一种我听不懂的语言喊叫了什么。接着四五名朝鲜人围住我，试图抓住我的手臂，因此我被迫使用警棍。
我看到其他警察也处于与我类似的境地，但我看不清具体是哪些人。几分钟后，朝鲜人被制服，并被逐出办公室进入大院，由费尔贝恩警司接管。
此致，
阁下之恭顺仆人，
J. Montgomery
副督察。

page_data.en:
Extract from Daily Report of Gordon Road Police
Station dated September 16, 1932.

Consular Court Proceedings.

At the Japanese Consular Court the case against the 31
Korean ex Bus inspectors was heard on the morning of 15-9-32
and remanded until 16-9-32. The persons charged were
released from custody.

Extract from Daily Report of Gordon Road Police
Station dated September 17, 1932.

Consular Court Proceedings.

On the 16-9-32 at the Japanese Consular Court the
hearing of the case against the Korean ex Bus inspectors was
continued, Police witnesses of the occurrence were cross
examined at length by the presiding Official the hearing
will be resumed this a.m. when Supt. Fairbairn and Inspector
Furness of Reserve Unit will be called to give evidence.
page_data.zh:
摘自1932年9月16日戈登路巡捕房日报。

领事法庭诉讼程序。

在日本领事法庭，针对31名朝鲜籍前巴士稽查员的案件于1932年9月15日上午审理，并延期至1932年9月16日。被控人员被解除羁押。

摘自1932年9月17日戈登路巡捕房日报。

领事法庭诉讼程序。

1932年9月16日，在日本领事法庭继续审理针对朝鲜籍前巴士稽查员的案件，事发时的警方证人受到主审官员的详细盘问，听证会将于今天上午恢复，届时将传唤预备队的费尔贝恩警司和弗内斯督察作证。

page_data.en:
Extract from the Morning State of Sept: 15, 1938.

A Riot Call was turned in at 5-52 p.m. by Sub/Inspector
Hancock attached to Gordon Road Station who reported trouble
at the General Omnibus Company Depot, Connaught Road.

The Riot Squads left the Reserve Unit at 5-54 p.m. under
the Charge of Inspt: Harness and arrived at the Bus Depot at
6-14 p.m. where Sub/Inspt: Hancock reported that there were
over thirty Koreans like Inspectors who refused to leave the
Building.

One Squad of Sikhs and eight Foreigners entered the
Building where Sub/Inspt: Hancock again requested the Koreans
who were all seated on the floor to leave, but they refused.

A Foreign Police Officer was about to lift one of the men
from the floor to eject him, when all the Koreans stood up,
stated, and commenced to assault the Police.

Supt: Fairbairn arrived on the Scene at the above time,
and gave an order for two Squads of Chinese to assist in

Mr. Shotter of the Bus Company stated that he wished to

摘自1938年9月15日晨间状态报告。

下午5点52分，隶属戈登路巡捕房的汉考克副督察发出骚乱呼叫，报告康纳路通用公共汽车公司车场发生麻烦。

防暴队于下午5点54分在哈尼斯（Harness）督察的率领下离开预备队，于下午6点14分抵达巴士车场，汉考克副督察报告称，有三十多名类似稽查员的朝鲜人拒绝离开大楼。

一支锡克教警员小队和八名外籍警员进入大楼，汉考克副督察再次请求所有坐在地上的朝鲜人离开，但他们拒绝了。

一名外籍警员正准备从地上拉起一人将其驱逐时，所有朝鲜人站了起来，叫喊着，并开始袭击警察。

费尔贝恩警司于上述时间抵达现场，并命令两支华捕队协助清理大楼，此举迅速完成。

巴士公司的肖特（Shotter）先生表示，他希望控告涉及的31名朝鲜人，随后这些人由预备队护送至戈登路巡捕房，并被拘留。

防暴队于下午7点12分返回预备队。

page_data.en:
Extract from Daily Report of Gordon Road Station
Dated September 15, 1932.

Subject: C.G.O. Co. Korean Ex-Inspectors.

Report: "At 4.45 p.m. 14-9-32 a telephone message was received
from Bus Co, reporting management were having trouble with
Korean ex-Inspectors. A party of Police attended under
S.I. Hancock and Firth, Mr. Shotter the Chief Engineer and
Manager was interviewed and he requested the Police to eject
these Koreans from the premises, as no agreement could be
arrived at between them. The Korean ex-Inspectors who were
assembled outside Mr. Shotter's Office numbering about 35
were then asked by the Police and advised to leave the
premises in a peaceful manner. They repeatedly stated that
they would like Mr. Shotter to answer a few more questions
and just as repeatedly were advised by the Police to leave
the premises. At 6.50 p.m. they were finally told to leave,
but point blankly refused. A riot call at approx. 6.50 p.m.
turned into the Reserve Unit who attended with the Musketry
Officer i/c of the operation of ejectment. This was
accomplished and resulted in 31 of their numbers being
arrested and brought to Gordon Road Station, subsequently
being transferred to the Japanese Consulate for detention,
14 were sent to Hospital of whom 8 were detained from minor
injuries whilst resisting the Police. Charges of Trespass
and Obstructing the Police are prepared against them and
the case will be heard in the Japanese Consular Court on
the 15/9/32."

日期：1932年9月15日。

事由：中国公共汽车公司（C.G.O. Co.）朝鲜籍前稽查员。

报告：“1932年9月14日下午4时45分，接到公共汽车公司电话报告，称管理层在与朝鲜籍前稽查员交涉时遇到麻烦。由副督察汉考克（Hancock）和弗思（Firth）率领的一队警员前往现场，首席工程师兼经理肖特先生（Mr. Shotter）接受了问询，他请求警方将这些朝鲜人驱逐出该处所，因为双方无法达成协议。聚集在肖特先生办公室外的朝鲜籍前稽查员约有35人，警方随即对他们进行劝告，建议他们和平离开该处所。他们反复表示希望肖特先生再回答几个问题，警方也反复劝告他们离开该处所。下午6时50分，警方最终命令他们离开，但他们断然拒绝。约下午6时50分发出的防暴呼叫调来了后备队，由负责驱逐行动的枪械教官带队。驱逐行动得以完成，结果其中31人被捕并带至戈登路捕房，随后被移送至日本领事馆拘留；另有14人被送往医院，其中8人因在抗拒警察时受轻伤而被拘留。已拟就非法侵入和阻碍警务两项指控，案件将于1932年9月15日在日本领事法庭审理。”

Subject (in full) Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus Company.

Made by F.P.S. 337 Vaughan-Neale. Forwarded by W.K. Fairbairn Supt.

Sir,
I beg to report that at 6.15 p.m. on the 14-9-32 I was instructed to accompany a party of 7 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs of the Riot Squad into the building of the above Company's Depot at Connaught Road for the purpose of ejecting 31 Koreans who had refused to leave the premises.
I proceeded to the first floor of the building and entered a room at the top of the staircase which was occupied by a number of Chinese, who were sitting upon the floor counting coppers. I decided that these were not the men complained of and upon leaving the room, continued to walk along a narrow passage, which after a few yards made a right angle turn to the left and within a very short distance again made a right angle turn to the right.
I noticed men were sitting on either side of the passage, but thinking they were employees waiting to go on duty, I continued to walk along the passage accompanied by two Sikhs. Suddenly I heard shouting and without warning the men seated on the floor of the passage jumped up raised their hands above their head, commenced shouting in a language I did not understand and charged at me.
I received several blows from the men and was finally kicked in the stomach. I called for assistance, but owing to about 20 Koreans were blocking the narrow passage, thus preventing anyone coming to my help. I was forced to used my baton and ordered my two Sikhs to do likewise, finally we forced our way back to the top of the staircase, where we were joined by other Police.
When the trouble had quietened down I proceeded down the stairs, and ordered two approaching squads of Chinese to return with me to the Depot Compound where Supt: Fairbairn took charge.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
C.F. Vaughan-Neale
F.P.S. 337

呈报人：外巡 337号 沃恩-尼尔（Vaughan-Neale）。转呈人：W.K·费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）总监。

先生，
谨此报告，1932年9月14日下午6时15分，我奉命随同防暴队的7名外籍警员和10名锡克族警员进入上述公司在康纳路的车场大楼，目的是驱逐31名拒绝离开该处所的朝鲜人。
我前往大楼二楼，进入楼梯顶端的一个房间，里面有许多中国人正坐在地上数铜板。我断定这些人并非被投诉的对象，于是离开房间，继续沿着一条狭窄的通道行走，该通道在几码后向左直角转弯，并在很短的距离内再次向右直角转弯。
我注意到通道两侧坐着一些人，但以为他们是等待上班的员工，便继续在两名锡克族警员的陪同下沿通道前行。突然，我听到喊叫声，毫无预警地，坐在通道地板上的人跳了起来，将手举过头顶，开始用我听不懂的语言喊叫，并向我也冲来。
我遭到这些人的数次殴打，最后腹部被踢了一脚。我呼救，但由于约20名朝鲜人堵塞了狭窄的通道，致使无人能前来相助。我被迫使用警棍，并命令我的两名锡克族警员也这样做，最终我们杀出一条血路回到楼梯顶端，与其他警察会合。
当骚乱平息后，我走下楼梯，命令两支援近的华警分队随我返回车场大院，由费尔贝恩总监接管指挥。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，
C.F. 沃恩-尼尔（Vaughan-Neale）
外巡 337号

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

报告

档案号................
后备队捕房，
日期 1932年9月15日：

事由（全称）关于从中国公共汽车公司驱逐31名朝鲜人之事。

呈报人：外巡 133号 史密斯（Smith）。转呈人：W·斯泰尔贝恩（Stairbain）总监。

先生，
1932年9月14日晚，后备队接到戈登路捕房的防暴呼叫，请求后备队在康纳路公共汽车公司提供协助，抵达后我们获悉，公共汽车公司的一栋建筑内有30多名朝鲜人，资方希望将其驱逐。后备队的外籍和锡克族警员以及戈登路捕房的一两名外籍警员被指派去要求朝鲜人离开该处所。随后我们前往他们占据的建筑，以礼貌的方式要求他们离开并给予了多次警告。当警察开始协助他们离开时，他们聚集在一起，在一段楼梯的顶部冲向警察，导致几人摔倒，在混乱中，警察被迫使用警棍以保护自己免受人身伤害。朝鲜人被带离该处所后，被送往戈登路捕房。

此致，
先生。
您顺从的仆人，

外巡 133号. W·史密斯（Smith）133

Form No. 2
G. 25,000-1-32

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ............
REPORT
Reserve Unit....Station,
Date 15th Sept .... 19 32

Subject (in full) Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus Depot.

Made by Inspector J. Furness. Forwarded by W.S. Fairbairn Supt.

Sir,
I beg to report that at 5.52 p.m. 14-9-32 a Riot Call was received from S.I. Hancock at the China General Omnibus Company, Connaught Road. The Riot Squads arrived at the above Depot at 6.14 p.m. when I was informed by S.I. Hancock that between 30 and 40 Korean ex Bus Inspectors were inside the building, and that although he had repeatedly requested them to leave, they refused to do so.

Mr Shotter of the Omnibus Company then requested me to have them ejected from the premises and stated that they had threatened to kill him, also that he was afraid that they would set fire to over 3,000 gallons of Gasoline which was stored on the premises.

Eight Foreigners and ten Sikhs of the Riot Squads were detailed to accompany S.I. Hancock inside the building, whilst I stayed with the Riot Van and took charge of the remaining two Chinese Squads. At this time Supt: Fairbairn arrived on the scene and took charge of operations.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. Furness
Inspector,
