档案号 ............
报告
后备队....捕房，
日期 1932年9月15日 .... 19 32年

事由（全称）关于从中国公共汽车车场驱逐31名朝鲜人之事。

呈报人：督察 J·弗内斯（Furness）。转呈人：W.S·费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）总监。

先生，
谨此报告，1932年9月14日下午5时52分，接到康纳路中国公共汽车公司副督察汉考克发出的防暴呼叫。防暴队于下午6时14分抵达上述车场，当时副督察汉考克告知我，大楼内有30至40名朝鲜籍前公共汽车稽查员，尽管他多次要求他们离开，但他们拒绝照办。

公共汽车公司的肖特先生随后请求我将他们驱逐出处所，并称他们曾威胁要杀害他，此外他还担心他们会纵火焚烧储存在该处所的超过3,000加仑汽油。

防暴队的八名外籍警员和十名锡克族警员被指派陪同副督察汉考克进入大楼，而我则留守防暴车并指挥其余两支华警分队。此时，费尔贝恩总监抵达现场并接管行动指挥。

此致，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J·弗内斯（Furness）
督察，

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit, Eastern Depot,
September 15, 1932.
Riot Call. Omnibus Co. Depot 14.9.32.

Commissioner.

Sir,

Further to the report on the Reserve Unit morning
State of September 15, 1932 (Copy attached):-

I arrived at the Omnibus Depot Connaught Rd. about
two minutes after the arrival of the Riot Squads and was
informed of the situation by Inspt. Furness. He also
informed me that there were a number of Foreigners and
Sikhs in the building.

I asked Mr. Shotter to accompany me into the building
where it was my intention to order the Koreans to leave.

Mr. Shotter said "Put them out" and something about
the Koreans having threatened him. I then entered the
building with Sub-Inspector Xu.

When half way up the stairs, (which was in darkness)
there were sounds of a free-for-all fight taking place on
the first floor. I immediately gave orders to the two
Chinese Squads to advance at the "Charge" and the building
was quickly cleared.

The Koreans were paraded in the Compound and informed
that they would be released two at a time providing they
went away quietly. Several of them were still in a fighting
mood and had to be restrained.

At that time Mr. Shotter came forward and said that
he was afraid that if the men were released that they would
create a disturbance outside on the roadway. I pointed out
that the Police were on private property and that we had no
charge against the men, and if the men did not disperse
when released the Police would quickly deal with them. Mr.
Shotter stated "I want the men charged and will prefer
charge against them".
page_data.zh:
后备队，东区分署，
1932年9月15日。
防暴呼叫。公共汽车公司车场 1932年9月14日。

警务处处长。

先生：

继1932年9月15日上午后备队状态报告之后（附副本）：-

我在防暴队抵达约两分钟后到达康纳路（Connaught Rd.）公共汽车车场，并由弗内斯督察（Inspt. Furness）告知现场情况。他还告诉我，大楼内有许多外国人和锡克人。

我请肖特先生（Mr. Shotter）随我进入大楼，我打算命令朝鲜人离开。

肖特先生说“把他们赶出去”，并提到朝鲜人曾威胁他。随后我与徐副督察（Sub-Inspector Xu）一同进入大楼。

当走到楼梯半腰时（楼梯上一片漆黑），听到一楼传来混战的声音。我立即命令两支华捕队发起“冲锋”，大楼很快被清空。

朝鲜人在大院内列队，并被告知只要他们安静离开，将每次释放两人。其中几人仍有斗殴情绪，不得不加以约束。

此时肖特先生走上前来说，他担心如果释放这些人，他们会在外面的道路上制造骚乱。我指出警察身处私人物业，且我们并未指控这些人，如果他们在获释后不散去，警察将迅速处置。肖特先生称：“我要控告这些人，并将对他们提出指控”。

page_data.en:
(2)

The men were then handed over to Sub-Inspt. Hancock
1/o Gordon Road District and an escort provided to take
them to Gordon Road Station.

The situation upon my arrival at the Omnibus Company
Depot was roughly as follows:-

(1) The Koreans had refused to obey the Police request
to leave the building for over an hour.
(2) They had threatened Mr. Shotter.
(3) They had talked about firing the Gasoline Tank.
(4) The building was in darkness (Light reported to have
been switched off by the Koreans).
(5) They were actually assaulting the Police who were
trying to peacefully remove them from the Building .

The Situation was such that I considered it necessary
to use quick and drastic methods to cope with it. The fact
that a few of them received minor injuries owing to this,
cannot under the circumstances be helped and it nothing more
than that must be expected to happen to anyone under like
circumstances.

It should be noted that the 8 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs
who entered the building with Sub-Inspt. Hancock, did so
with their batons in their pockets etc. and had the Koreans
not assaulted the police they would not have been injured.

The Police only used sufficient force to effectively
deal with the situation.

(Sd) W.E. Fairbairn,
Superintendent.
page_data.zh:
(2)

随后，这些人被移交给戈登路区（Gordon Road District）的汉考克副督察（Sub-Inspt. Hancock），并安排护送人员将他们带往戈登路捕房。

我抵达公共汽车公司车场时的情况大致如下：-

(1) 朝鲜人拒绝服从警方要求离开大楼的命令已超过一小时。
(2) 他们威胁了肖特先生。
(3) 他们扬言要点燃汽油罐。
(4) 大楼内一片漆黑（据报灯光系被朝鲜人关闭）。
(5) 他们实际上正在袭击试图和平将他们移出大楼的警察。

鉴于局势如此，我认为有必要采取快速且严厉的措施来应对。因此导致其中少数人受轻伤，在这种情况下是不可避免的，而且在类似情况下，任何人遭遇此类事情都是意料之中的。

需要注意的是，随汉考克副督察进入大楼的8名外国人和10名锡克人，是将警棍放在口袋等处的，如果朝鲜人没有袭击警察，他们是不会受伤的。

警方仅使用了足以有效处理局势的必要武力。

（签名）W.E. 费尔贝恩（W.E. Fairbairn），
警司。

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit,
September 16, 1930.

Disturbance at the China General Omnibus Company's Depot
Connaught Road on September 14, 1930.

Sir,

I beg to report that on September 14, 1930 in response to a
'kist call, I accompanied the riot squad, Inspector Furness in
charge, to the above mentioned premises, arriving there at 6.14 p.m.
In the compound of the Depot there were a number of police
officers amongst which was Sub-Inspector Hancock. The latter
informed Inspector Furness that about 30 Korean ex-employees had
taken up position in the company's offices and refused to leave
the premises when requested to do so by the management and the
police, and that assistance was required in evicting them.
Eight foreigners and ten Sikhs of the riot squad were ordered
to accompany Sub-Inspector Hancock to the offices to deal with the
Koreans. I accompanied the police party to the first floor of the
Company's offices and in a narrow passage at the head of the stairs
perceived a number of Koreans sitting on the floor. I heard some-
one advise them to leave the premises, this was followed by the
sound of a struggle, but as the light was bad, I could not see
who was actually engaged.
I then hold of the arm of one of the Koreans who was sitting
on the floor and endeavoured to get him to his feet, at the same
time telling him to get out. The Korean said "No-No", and shouted
something in a language I did not understand. Four or five Koreans
then crowded round me and tried to get hold of my arms and I was
therefore compelled to use my baton.
I saw that other police officers were placed in a similar
position to myself but I could not see who the individuals were.
In a few minutes the Koreans were subdued and were put out
of the offices into the compound where Supt. Fairbairn took charge.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(sd.) J. Montgomery.
Sub-Inspector.
page_data.zh:
后备队，
1930年9月16日。

1930年9月14日中华公共汽车公司康纳路车场骚乱事件。

先生：

谨此报告，1930年9月14日，响应一次“kist call”（原文不清，疑似指紧急呼叫或笔误），我陪同由弗内斯督察（Inspector Furness）负责的防暴队前往上述地点，于下午6点14分抵达。在车场大院内有多名警务人员，其中包括汉考克副督察（Sub-Inspector Hancock）。后者告知弗内斯督察，约有30名朝鲜籍前雇员占据了公司办公室，并在管理层和警方要求离开时拒绝撤离，因此需要协助将其驱逐。
防暴队中的八名外国人和十名锡克人奉命陪同汉考克副督察前往办公室处理朝鲜人。我随警务人员来到公司办公室的一楼，在楼梯顶端的狭窄过道里，看到几名朝鲜人坐在地板上。我听到有人劝他们离开该处所，随后传来搏斗声，但由于光线昏暗，我无法看清实际参与搏斗者是谁。
随后我抓住一名坐在地上的朝鲜人的手臂，试图让他站起来，同时叫他出去。该朝鲜人说“不-不”，并用一种我听不懂的语言喊叫。接着四五名朝鲜人围住我，试图抓住我的手臂，因此我被迫使用警棍。
我看到其他警务人员也处于与我类似的境地，但我看不清具体是哪些人。
几分钟后，朝鲜人被制服，并被从办公室赶到大院，由费尔贝恩警司（Supt. Fairbairn）接管。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）J. 蒙哥马利（J. Montgomery）。
副督察。

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit,
September 16, 1932.

Disturbance at the China General Omnibus Company's Depot
Connaught Road on September 14, 1932.

Sir,

I beg to report that on September 14, 1932 in response to a
Riot Call, I accompanied the Riot Squad, Inspector Furness in
charge, to the above mentioned premises, arriving there at 6.14 p.m.

In the compound of the Depot there were a number of Police
officers amongst which was Sub-Inspector Hancock. The latter
informed Inspector Furness that about 35 Korean ex-employees had
taken up position in the Company's offices and refused to leave
the premises when requested to do so by the management and the
Police, and that assistance was required in evicting them.

Eight Foreigners and ten Sikhs of the Riot Squad were ordered
to accompany Sub-Inspector Hancock to the offices to deal with the
Koreans. I accompanied the Police party to the first floor of the
Company's offices and in a narrow passage at the head of the stairs
perceived a number of Koreans sitting on the floor. I heard some-
one advise them to leave the premises, this was followed by the
sound of a struggle, but as the light was bad, I could not see
who was actually engaged.

I then hold of the arm of one of the Koreans who was sitting
on the floor and endeavoured to get him to his feet, at the same
time telling him to get out. The Korean said "No-No", and shouted
something in a language I did not understand. Four or five Koreans
then crowded round me and tried to get hold of my arms and I was
therefore compelled to use my baton.

I saw that other Police officers were placed in a similar
position to myself but I could not see who the individuals were.

In a few minutes the Koreans were subdued and were put out
of the offices into the compound where Supt. Fairbairn took charge.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(sd.) J. Montgomery.

Sub-Inspector.
page_data.zh:
后备队，
1932年9月16日。

关于1932年9月14日康纳路（Connaught Road）中国公共汽车公司车厂骚乱事件。

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年9月14日，为响应防暴呼叫，我随同由弗内斯（Furness）巡官率领的防暴队前往上述地点，于下午6时14分抵达。

在车厂大院内有多名警务人员，其中包括汉考克（Hancock）副巡官。后者告知弗内斯巡官，约有35名韩国籍前雇员占据了公司办公室，并在管理层和警方要求离开时拒绝撤离，因此需要协助将其驱逐。

防暴队中的八名外籍警员和十名锡克族警员奉命陪同汉考克副巡官前往办公室处理韩国人一事。我随同警方人员来到公司办公室的一楼，在楼梯顶端的狭窄通道里，我看到一些韩国人坐在地板上。我听到有人劝他们离开现场，随后传来扭打的声音，但由于光线昏暗，我无法看清实际参与扭打的是谁。

随后，我抓住一名坐在地上的韩国人的手臂，试图让他站起来，同时叫他出去。该韩国人说“不—不”，并用一种我听不懂的语言喊叫。接着，四五名韩国人围住我，试图抓住我的手臂，因此我被迫使用警棍。

我看到其他警务人员也陷入了与我类似的处境，但我看不清具体是哪些人。

几分钟后，韩国人被制服，并被从办公室赶到大院，由费尔贝恩（Fairbairn） superintendent 接管。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人，

（签名）J. 蒙哥马利（J. Montgomery）。

副巡官。

page_data.en:
Extract from the Morning State of September 15, 1932.

A Riot Call was turned in at 5.52 p.m. by Sub-Inspector
Hancock attached to Gordon Road Station who reported trouble
at the General Omnibus Company Depot, Connaught Road.

The Riot Squads left the Reserve Unit at 5.54 p.m. under
the Charge of Inspector Furness and arrived at the Bus Depot at
6.14 p.m. where Sub-Inspector Hancock reported that there were
over thirty Koreans, Ex Inspectors who refused to leave the
Building.

One Squad of Sikhs and eight Foreigners entered the
Building where Sub-Inspector Hancock again requested the
Koreans who were all seated on the floor to leave, but they
refused.

A Foreign Police Officer was about to lift one of the men
from the floor to eject him, when all the Koreans stood up,
stated, and commenced to assault the Police.

Supt. Fairbairn arrived on the scene at the above time,
and gave an order for two Squads of Chinese to assist in
cleaning the Building, which was done in quick time.

Mr. Shotter of the Bus Company stated that he wished to
lay a charge against the 31 Koreans concerned the men were then
escorted by the Reserve Unit to Gordon Road Station, where
they were detained.

The Riot Squads returned to the Reserve Unit at 7.12 p.m.
page_data.zh:
摘自1932年9月15日的晨间状况报告。

下午5时52分，戈登路（Gordon Road）警署的汉考克（Hancock）副巡官发出防暴呼叫，报告康纳路（Connaught Road）公共汽车公司车厂发生骚乱。

防暴队于下午5时54分在弗内斯（Furness）巡官的率领下离开后备队，于下午6时14分抵达公交车库，汉考克副巡官报告称，有三十多名韩国籍前巡长拒绝离开大楼。

一队锡克族警员和八名外籍警员进入大楼，汉考克副巡官再次要求所有坐在地上的韩国人离开，但他们拒绝了。

一名外籍警员正打算将其中一人从地上拉起以将其驱逐，此时所有韩国人站了起来，叫喊并开始袭击警察。

费尔贝恩（Fairbairn） superintendent 于上述时间抵达现场，命令两支华捕队协助清理大楼，此事迅速完成。

公交公司的肖特（Shotter）先生表示，他希望起诉涉及的31名韩国人，这些人随后由后备队护送至戈登路（Gordon Road）警署，并在那里被拘留。

防暴队于下午7时12分返回后备队。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT.

Reserve Unit,
Date 15th Sept. 1932.

Subject (in full) Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General
Omnibus Company.

Made by F.P.S.133 Smith. forwarded by W.E. Fairbairn, Supt.

Sir,

On the evening of the 14th Sept. 1932, the Reserve Unit
received a Riot Call from Gordon Road Police Station asking the
services of the Unit at the Bus Company at Connaught Road, on
arriving there we were informed that there were over 30 Koreans
in one of the Bus Company's Buildings whom they wished to be
ejected. The Foreign and Sikh Police from the Reserve Unit with
one or two Foreigners from Gordon Road Station were detailed to
ask the Koreans to leave the premises. We then proceeded to the
building which they occupied, they were then asked in a civil
manner to leave and given several warnings. When Police started
to assist them to leave they got together and rushed at the Police
at the top of a flight of stairs of which several men fell down,
during the scramble the Police were compelled to use their batons
to defend themselves from bodily harm. When the Koreans were
removed from the premises they were taken to Gordon Road Police
Station.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(sd). F.P.S. 133. W. Smith.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

报告。

后备队，
日期：1932年9月15日。

主题（全称）：关于从中国公共汽车公司驱逐31名韩国人一事。

由外籍警员编号133史密斯（Smith）撰写。由 superintendent W.E. 费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）转呈。

阁下：

1932年9月14日晚，后备队接到戈登路（Gordon Road）警署的防暴呼叫，请求派员前往康纳路（Connaught Road）的公交公司。抵达后，我们获悉公交公司的一栋大楼内有30多名韩国人，当局希望将其驱逐。后备队的外籍和锡克族警员，以及戈登路（Gordon Road）警署的一两名外籍警员，被指派去要求韩国人离开现场。随后我们前往他们占据的大楼，以礼貌的方式要求他们离开，并给予了多次警告。当警察开始协助他们离开时，他们聚集在一起，在一段楼梯的顶部冲向警察，导致数人摔倒。在混乱中，警察被迫使用警棍以保护自身免受身体伤害。韩国人被带离现场后，被送往戈登路（Gordon Road）警署。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）外籍警员编号133. W. 史密斯（W. Smith）。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

Reserve Unit.
Date 15th Sept. 1932.

Subject (in full) Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus
Company.

Made by P.S. 314 Douglas. forwarded by W.E. Fairbairn Supt.

Sir,

On the evening of the 14th Sept. 1932 I attended the Riot Call
from the Reserve Unit (E) at the China General Omnibus Company,
Connaught Road. I was instructed along with other Foreigners to
eject about 40 Koreans who were sitting on the landing outside the
Company's office on the first floor. They were told to leave the
premises, no force being used and refused to move, and on being
touched became violent and attempted to rush the Police, we were
then forced to use our batons in self defence, before we were able
to eject them.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(sd) P.S. 314 J. Douglas.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

后备队。
日期：1932年9月15日。

主题（全称）：关于从中国公共汽车公司驱逐31名韩国人一事。

由警员编号314道格拉斯（Douglas）撰写。由 superintendent W.E. 费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）转呈。

阁下：

1932年9月14日晚，我响应来自后备队（E队）的防暴呼叫，前往康纳路（Connaught Road）的中国公共汽车公司。我与其他外籍警员一起受命驱逐约40名坐在该公司一楼办公室外平台上的韩国人。被告知离开现场时，未使用武力，但他们拒绝移动，且在受到触碰时变得暴力并试图冲击警察，我们随后被迫在驱逐他们之前使用警棍进行自卫。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人，

（签名）警员编号314 J. 道格拉斯（J. Douglas）。

REPORT.

Reserve Unit.
Date 15th Sept. 1932.
Subject (in full) Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General
Omnibus Company.
Made by F.P.S. 81 Burt. forwarded by W.E. Fairbairn Supt.

Sir,

I beg to report that on the night of the 14th Sept. 1932 I
attended a Riot Call from the Bus Company, Connaught Road.
On arrival we were told that about 40 Koreans were inside the
shed and refused to leave.
After hearing them asked to go were asked to eject them.
The Koreans were sitting on the floor and on the first being
stood up the rest all jumped to their feet with a big yell and
rushed the Police that were there and to avoid injury the Police
had to resort to the use of batons, which on entering the shed
we all had in our baton pockets.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(sd) F.P.S. 81 S.E. Burt.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

由外籍警员编号81伯特（Burt）撰写。由 superintendent W.E. 费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）转呈。

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年9月14日晚，我响应康纳路（Connaught Road）公交公司的防暴呼叫。抵达后，我们被告知约有40名韩国人在棚屋内，拒绝离开。
在听到要求他们离开的指令后，我们受命将其驱逐。
韩国人坐在地板上，当第一人站起来时，其余的人全都跳起来，大声叫喊，并冲向在场的警察。为避免受伤，警察不得不使用警棍，我们在进入棚屋时都将警棍放在警棍袋中。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人，

（签名）外籍警员编号81 S.E. 伯特（S.E. Burt）。

REPORT.

Reserve Unit.
Date 15th Sept. 1932.

Subject (in full) Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus
Company.

Made by F.P.S. 85 Massey. Forwarded by W.E. Fairbairn Supt.

Sir,

I beg to report that on the 14th Sept. 1932 I attended the
Riot Call at the above Company's Depot. At about 6.15 p.m. we
arrived at the Depot, where I and about eight Foreigners were
instructed to enter the building and eject with the least possible
force about 35 Koreans who were sitting on the floor, we endeavoured
to carry out our instructions, but the Koreans jumped to their feet
shouting and resisting the Police, making it necessary to use
force in ejecting them.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant.

(sd) F.P.S. 85 F.H. Massey.

主题（全称）：关于从中国公共汽车公司驱逐31名韩国人一事。

由外籍警员编号85梅西（Massey）撰写。由 superintendent W.E. 费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）转呈。

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年9月14日，我响应上述公司车厂的防暴呼叫。大约在下午6时15分，我们抵达车厂，我和大约八名外籍警员受命进入大楼，以尽可能小的武力驱逐约35名坐在地上的韩国人。我们努力执行指令，但韩国人跳起来叫喊并抵抗警察，使得在驱逐他们时必须使用武力。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人。

（签名）外籍警员编号85 F.H. 梅西（F.H. Massey）。

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit,
15th September 1932.

Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus Depot.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 5.52 p.m. 14-9-32 a Riot Call was received from S.I. Hancock at the China General Omnibus Company, Connaught Road. The Riot Squads arrived at the above Depot at 6.14 p.m. when I was informed by S.I. Hancock that between 30 and 40 Korean ex Bus Inspectors were inside the building, and that although he had repeatedly requested them to leave, they refused to do so.

Mr. Shotter of the Omnibus Company then requested me to have them ejected from the premises and stated that they had threatened to kill him, also that he was afraid that they would set fire to over 3,000 gallons of Gasoline which was stored on the premises.

Eight Foreigners and ten Sikhs of the Riot Squads were detailed to accompany S.I. Hancock inside the building, whilst I stayed with the Riot Van and took charge of the remaining two Chinese Squads. At this time Supt. Fairbairn arrived on the scene and took charge of operations.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(sd.) J. Furness,
Inspector.
page_data.zh:
后备队，
1932年9月15日。

关于从中国公共汽车车厂驱逐31名韩国人一事。

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年9月14日下午5时52分，收到康纳路（Connaught Road）中国公共汽车公司汉考克（Hancock）副巡官发出的防暴呼叫。防暴队于下午6时14分抵达上述车厂，当时汉考克（Hancock）副巡官告知我，大楼内有30至40名韩国籍前公交车巡长，尽管他多次要求他们离开，但他们拒绝这样做。

公交公司的肖特（Shotter）先生随后请求我将他们逐出场地，并称他们曾威胁要杀死他，此外他还担心他们会纵火焚烧储存在场地内的3000多加仑汽油。

防暴队中的八名外籍警员和十名锡克族警员被指派陪同汉考克（Hancock）副巡官进入大楼，而我则留守防暴车，并指挥其余的两支华捕队。此时，费尔贝恩（Fairbairn） superintendent 抵达现场并接管行动指挥。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）J. 弗内斯（J. Furness），
巡官。

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit.
September 15, 1932.

Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus Company.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 6.15 p.m. on the 14-9-32 I was instructed
to accompany a party of 7 Foreigners and 10 Sikhs of the Riot Squad
into the building of the above Company's Depot at Connaught Road
for the purpose of ejecting 31 Koreans who had refused to leave the
premises.

I proceeded to the first floor of the building and entered a
room at the top of the staircase which was occupied by a number of
Chinese, who were sitting upon the floor counting coppers. I decided
that these were not the men complained of and upon leaving the room,
continued to walk along a narrow passage, which after a few yards
made a right angle turn to the left and within a very short distance
against a right angle turn to the right.

I noticed men were sitting on either side of the passage, but
thinking they were employees waiting to go on duty, I continued to
walk along the passage accompanied by two Sikhs. Suddenly I heard
shouting and without warning the men seated on the floor of the
passage jumped up raised their hands above their head, commenced
shouting in a language I did not understand and charged at me.

I received several blows from the men and was finally kicked
in the stomach. I called for assistance, but owing to about 20
Koreans were blocking the narrow passage, thus preventing anyone
coming to my help. I was forced to used my baton and ordered my two
Sikhs to do likewise, finally we forced our way back to the top of
the staircase, where we were joined by other Police.

When the trouble had quietened down I proceeded down the stairs,
and ordered two approaching squads of Chinese to return with me to
the Depot Compound where Supt. Fairbairn took charge.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(sd.) C.G. Vaughan-Neale.
F.P.S. 337
page_data.zh:
后备队。
1932年9月15日。

关于从中国公共汽车公司驱逐31名韩国人一事。

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年9月14日下午6时15分，我受命陪同由7名外籍警员和10名锡克族防暴队员组成的小组，进入康纳路（Connaught Road）上述公司车厂的大楼，目的是驱逐31名拒绝离开现场的韩国人。

我前往大楼的一楼，进入楼梯顶端的一个房间，里面有一些中国人正坐在地板上数铜板。我断定这些人并非被投诉的对象，于是离开房间，继续沿着一条狭窄的通道行走，该通道在几码后向左直角转弯，又在很短的距离内向右直角转弯。

我注意到通道两侧坐着一些人，但以为他们是等待上班的员工，便继续沿着通道前行，两名锡克族警员随行。突然，我听到叫喊声，毫无预警地，坐在通道地板上的人跳了起来，将手举过头顶，开始用我听不懂的语言叫喊，并向冲来。

我遭到这些人的数次殴打，最后腹部被踢了一脚。我呼叫援助，但由于约20名韩国人堵塞了狭窄的通道，阻止任何人前来帮助我。我被迫使用警棍，并命令我的两名锡克族警员也这样做，最终我们杀回楼梯顶部，与其他警察会合。

当骚乱平息后，我走下楼梯，命令两支正在靠近的华捕队随我返回车厂大院，由费尔贝恩（Fairbairn） superintendent 接管。

阁下，
您顺从的仆人，

（签名）C.G. 沃恩-尼尔（Vaughan-Neale）。
外籍警员编号337

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit,
September 15, 1932.

Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus Company.

Sir,
    I beg to report that I attended the Riot Call at the Bus
Company, Connaught Road at 6.15 p.m. on the 14th Sept. 1932 and on
arriving was instructed to go with about 8 other Foreigners upstairs
where there was about 40 Koreans sitting on the floor and eject
them from the building. This we tried to do after giving them
sufficient warning and using as little force as possible, whereupon
they refused to move and became very violent and attempt to rush
the Police, we were then compelled to use our batons in self defence
before we could eject them.

                        I am, Sir,
                        Your obedient servant,

                        (sd.) H.J. Beer.
                        F.S. 224.

阁下，
    谨此报告，1932年9月14日下午6时15分，我响应康纳路（Connaught Road）公交公司的防暴呼叫，抵达后受命与其他约8名外籍警员一起上楼，那里约有40名韩国人坐在地板上，需将他们逐出大楼。在给予充分警告并尽可能少使用武力的情况下，我们尝试这样做，但他们拒绝移动并变得非常暴力，试图冲击警察，我们随后被迫在驱逐他们之前使用警棍进行自卫。

                        阁下，
                        您顺从的仆人，

                        （签名）H.J. 比尔（Beer）。

page_data.en:
Reserve Unit,
September 15, 1932.

Re 31 Koreans ejected from the China General Omnibus Coy.

Sir,

I beg to report that the alarm bell was rung at 5.52 p.m.
on the 14-9-32 and we proceeded to the Omnibus Company at Connaught
Road and on arriving there a squad of Foreigners including myself
and a squad of Sikhs were given orders by Inspector Furness to
proceed upstairs to eject some Koreans who were at that time
sitting on the floor.

They had been given ample time and warning to remove
themselves from the premises but they refused, on entering they
jumped up in a threatening attitude and we had to remove them
downstairs by force, where they were arrested and taken to Gordon
Road Police Station.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(sd.) W.C.J. Bloomfield
F.S. 137.

1932年9月15日。

关于被中国公共汽车公司驱逐的31名朝鲜人一事。

先生：

谨此报告，1932年9月14日下午5时52分警铃响起，我们随即前往康纳路（Connaught Road）的公共汽车公司。抵达后，弗内斯（Furness）巡官命令由我带领的一队外籍警员以及一队锡克警员上楼，驱逐当时正坐在地板上的若干朝鲜人。

此前已给予他们充足的时间和警告，要求他们离开该处所，但他们予以拒绝。当我们进入时，他们以威胁性的姿态跳起，我们不得不强行将他们带至楼下，随后将其逮捕并押往戈登路警察局。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）W.C.J. 布卢姆菲尔德
警号 137。

Disturbance at office of the China General Omnibus
Company on October 14. - Ref. C. 6147/1 of 13-10-...

... in the course of this incident ... for re-
... to be found in the files ... of Oc-
tober 1, 16 and 17. I do not propose to traverse the
report forwarded by the Consul-General for Japan in its
entirety as a great part of it is concerned with the events
leading up to the incident on September 14, which should,
in my opinion, be taken as it stands.

On the day in question a foreign sergeant and two Chinese
constables were on duty at the main entrance to the Bus
Company's property on ... Road with instructions to
prevent any attempt on the part of a body of Korean dismissed
inspectors to force their way into the compound. At about
4.30 p.m., however, the Korean ex-inspectors to the number of
about 30 forced their way past the police on duty and demanded
an interview with Mr. Shotter, the Chief Engineer of the
Company. After some discussion six of the Koreans were
admitted to an interview with Mr. Shotter while the remainder
seated themselves on the floor of the passage leading to his
office. In the meantime the matter had been reported to
Gordon Road Police Station both by the Foreign Sergeant on
duty and by Mr. Shotter who stated that the Bus Company were
having trouble with the Korean ex-inspectors. A party of

……在此事件过程中……重新
……可在档案中找到……10
月1日、16日和17日的。我不打算全面复述日本总领事转来的报告，因为其中大部分内容涉及导致9月14日事件发生的前因，我认为这部分内容应维持原状予以接受。

在事发当日，一名外籍警长和两名华捕在公共汽车公司位于……路物业的主入口处执勤，接到的指令是防止一群被解雇的朝鲜籍查票员强行闯入大院。然而，大约在下午4时30分，约30名朝鲜前查票员强行冲过执勤警察的防线，并要求与公司总工程师肖特（Shotter）先生面谈。经过一番讨论，六名朝鲜人被允许与肖特先生面谈，其余人员则坐在通往其办公室的通道地板上。与此同时，执勤的外籍警长和肖特先生均向戈登路警察局报告了此事，肖特先生表示公共汽车公司在与朝鲜前查票员的交涉中遇到了麻烦。一队

page_data.en:
2.
police consisting of four foreigners and 12 Chinese attended
and the officer in charge, Sub-Inspector Hancock, was re-
quested to eject the Koreans as no agreement could be reached
between them and the Company. The police then requested and
advised the Koreans to leave the premises peacefully but
this they refused to do. At 5.50 p.m. when the police had
been there nearly an hour the men were ordered to leave, but
refused to do so. Sub-Inspector Hancock, not wishing to
arouse racial animosity by using the police he then had with
him, obtained the assistance of the Reserve Unit in accord-
ance with the procedure laid down for obtaining that assist-
ance. It should here be pointed out that the Reserve Unit
exists for the purpose of dealing with crowds, disorderly
gatherings and any situation with which it is considered
that the ordinary available police on duty are unable to
deal. During the past six years the Unit has frequently
been called out in connection with labour disputes in mills
and factories where employees and ex-employees endeavour to
intimidate the management and where it is necessary for the
preservation of lives and property to eject the labourers or
employees from the mill premises. In such cases a show of
force generally achieves the desired result, but this not
always the case and when resistance is offered the police,
who are specially trained for this sort of work, have to
use force. When force is used on such occasions a certain
number of persons are bound to receive injuries.
On the arrival of the Reserve Unit at 6.14 p.m. the
Officer in charge was informed of the situation and leaving
his Chinese, to the number of 26, in the compound sent eight
foreigners and 10 Sikhs with their batons in their pockets
to the building where Mr. Shotter's office is situated in
order to eject the Koreans. As the men entered the build-
ing Superintendent Fairbairn, who was not at the barracks
when the call for assistance was received, arrived and took
charge. As soon as the police party entered the building
page_data.zh:
2.
由四名外籍警员和12名华捕组成的警察队伍赶到，负责警官汉考克（Hancock）副巡官被要求驱逐这些朝鲜人，因为他们与公司之间无法达成协议。警方随后请求并建议朝鲜人和平离开该处所，但他们拒绝这样做。下午5时50分，即警方到达近一小时后，警员们奉命离开，但遭到拒绝。汉考克副巡官不愿因使用当时随行的警察而激起种族对立情绪，遂按照既定的求援程序，请求后备队协助。此处需指出，后备队的设立旨在处理人群、无序集会以及任何被认为当值常规警力无法应对的局面。在过去六年中，该队经常因工厂劳资纠纷而被调遣，在这些纠纷中，雇员和前雇员试图恐吓管理层，且为了保全生命和财产，有必要将劳工或雇员逐出厂区。在此类情况下，展示武力通常能达到预期效果，但并非总是如此；当遭遇抵抗时，受过专门训练以应对此类工作的警察不得不使用武力。在此类场合使用武力时，必然会有不少人受伤。
后备队于下午6时14分抵达，负责警官获悉情况后，将26名华捕留在大院内，派遣八名外籍警员和10名锡克警员，警棍插在口袋中，前往肖特先生办公室所在的建筑物，以驱逐朝鲜人。当警员们进入建筑物时，费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）总监（他在接到求援呼叫时不在营房）抵达并接管指挥。警察队伍一进入建筑物

page_data.en:
3.
which was in darkness, a shout arose and it was obvious that
the police were meeting with resistance. Superintendent
Airbairn then ordered his Chinese, who were drawn up in the
compound, to charge. This is one of the stages in the
ordinary drill carried out by the Reserve Unit and the men
are trained to cheer when they charge, such an action having
a distinct psychological effect on crowds. There was nothing
particularly unusual about the situation, which was dealt
with in the same manner as have been many others and I cannot
see why it should be treated differently.

The evidence of the police officers from Gordon Road
Police Station, who first came in contact with the Korean
ex-inspectors, is that their attitude was a blank refusal
to carry out the suggestions, advice and finally orders of
the Police. As soon as an attempt was made to lift up one
of the ex-inspectors his comrades seemed to lose their heads
and their attitude was one of defiance of the police. This
being the case, those who received injuries have only them-
selves to blame and the Council or police can accept no
responsibility in the matter.

The Procurator of the Japanese Consular Court endeavours
to make out that the ex-inspectors were peacefully disposed,
an allegation which can be applied to most crowds in the
early stages. The fact that 25 out of the 31 Koreans in-
volved are known to be subscribers to the Korean Provisional
Government in the French Concession and other reactionary
organisations hardly bears out the contention that they were
merely peaceful Japanese subjects.

I omitted to state that the information given to the
members of the Reserve Unit by Mr. Shotter on their arrival
was that the men had threatened to kill him and to set fire
to 3,000 gallons of gasoline which was stored in the compound.
Faced with this report it was obvious that the police had to
act with celerity and firmness and their action, in my
opinion, was fully justified.
page_data.zh:
3.
由于楼内一片漆黑，喊叫声四起，显然警察遭遇了抵抗。费尔贝恩总监随即命令集结在大院内的华捕发起冲锋。这是后备队常规操练中的一个环节，警员们受训在冲锋时呐喊，这种行动对人群具有明显的心理震慑作用。当时的情况并无特别异常之处，处理方式也与以往许多类似情况相同，我看不出为何要对此区别对待。

首先与朝鲜前查票员接触的戈登路警察局警官们的证词表明，他们的态度是一概拒绝执行警方的建议、劝告乃至最终的命令。一旦试图抬起其中一名前查票员，他的同伴们似乎就失去了理智，表现出对抗警方的态度。既然如此，那些受伤的人只能怪咎自身，工部局或警方对此不承担任何责任。

日本领事法院的检察官试图声称这些前查票员性情平和，这种说法在大多数人群事件的初期阶段或许适用。然而，涉案的31名朝鲜人中有25人已知是法租界朝鲜临时政府及其他反动组织的资助者，这一事实很难支持他们仅仅是和平的日本臣民这一论点。

我遗漏说明的一点是，肖特先生在后备队成员抵达时向他们提供的信息是，这些人曾威胁要杀死他，并点燃储存在大院内的3,000加仑汽油。面对这一报告，警方显然必须迅速而坚定地采取行动，在我看来，他们的行动是完全正当的。

page_data.en:
4.

I have received from Dr. Tongu of the Foo Ming Hospital
a demand for payment of $1,058 for hospital treatment of 11
men who were detained in that hospital and 6 who received
treatment as out-patients. This bill is made out on the
assumption that the Council will be responsible for the pay-
ment of these expenses. A Japanese Sergeant is alleged to
have informed Dr. Tongu to this effect but I am satisfied
that no such statement was made by foreigners nor by any
Japanese member of the Force. I propose replying to Dr.
Tongu disclaiming all responsibility in the matter but shall
not do so until I have received further instructions in con-
nection with the letter from the Japanese Consul-General dated
October 17.

(Sd.)
Extra Commissioner of Police.

（批：In my view at the time when the
Koreans in remaining on the premises refused
to leave when asked to do so this was in order
to intimidate persons committing an offence of
criminal trespass whether or not they expected by
the Police a more serious altercation would have
arisen. The Police used no more force than was
necessary in the circumstances. I do not agree
that they exceeded their duty. Nor am I certain
there are grounds for action against any of the
Police concerned in the affair.
Sd.
7/11.）

（左侧边注：Reply
11/11
JR）

4.

我已收到福明医院（Foo Ming Hospital）唐古（Tongu，音译）医生提出的支付1,058美元的要求，用于支付在该医院拘留治疗的11人及作为门诊接受治疗的6人的医疗费用。这份账单是基于工部局将负责支付这些费用的假设开具的。据称一名日本警长曾向唐古医生如此告知，但我确信没有任何外籍警员或任何日籍警员做过此类陈述。我拟回复唐古医生，声明在此事上不承担任何责任，但在收到有关日本总领事10月17日来函的进一步指示之前，暂不发出此回复。

（签名）
警务处额外专员。

（批注：在我看来，当时朝鲜人滞留现场并在被要求离开时拒绝离开，其目的是为了恐吓他人，这构成了非法侵入罪。无论他们是否预料到警方会介入，更严重的冲突本可能发生。警方在当时情况下使用的武力并未超过必要限度。我不同意他们超越了职责范围。我也不确定是否有理由对参与此事的任何警员采取纪律行动。
签名
11月7日。）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Gordon Road Station,
REPORT
(1)
Date October 25th 1932

Subject (in full) Attached

Made by S.I. Hancock Forwarded by C.W. Biggs.

Sir,
Re the attached, the following comments are offered by
S.I. Hancock, S.I. Firth and F.S. 138 Ball:
The 27 Koreans did not just simply enter the Bus Coy. pre-
mises in a peaceful manner but forced their way past F.S. Ball on
duty at the gate, although he requested them to wait outside. F.S.
Ball acted on his own initiative in placing two C.P.Cs. on duty
in the corridor, and not at the request of the management. He did
this as he feared the Koreans might get troublesome as they were
all very excited and in this corridor there is a lot of glass
windows.
Mr. Shotter did not request S.I. Hancock to eject all the
Koreans except six, he definately asked that they all be ejected
as he did not wish to discuss the matter further. S.I. Hancock
did not find himself at a loss what to do, but exercised great
patience, and gave them more than one hour in the hopes that they would
leave peacefully. After more than one hour of trying to pur-
suade them to leave he came to the conclusion that any further
effort to obtain a peaceful settlement, would be useless, there-
fore he called upon the Riot Squad. He did this as he wanted to
avoid if possible, any clash between the Chinese Police and
Koreans. Racial feelings had already been aroused as S.I.
Hancock was aware by having heard remarks being passed by the
Chinese Police. By calling upon the Riot Squad more Foreign Police
would be available doing away with the necessity of using the
Chinese Police, and that is exactly what happened, only Foreign
Police were used to eject the Koreans. Some Indian Police did go
upstairs but they took no part in the ejectment.
On arrival of Riot Squad S.I. Hancock reported the situation

来自 2

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案编号............
戈登路警局，
报告
(1)
日期 1932年10月25日

主题（完整）见附件

由汉考克副巡官制作，由C.W. 比格斯（Biggs）转发。

先生：
关于附件，汉考克副巡官、弗思（Firth）副巡官及警号138鲍尔（Ball）提出以下评论：
这27名朝鲜人并非仅仅以和平方式进入公共汽车公司物业，而是强行冲过在门口执勤的鲍尔警员，尽管他要求他们在外面等候。鲍尔警员主动安排两名华捕在走廊执勤，而非应管理层要求。他这样做是因为担心朝鲜人可能会惹出麻烦，因为他们都非常激动，而且这条走廊里有很多玻璃窗。
肖特先生并未要求汉考克副巡官只驱逐除六人以外的所有朝鲜人，他明确要求将所有人员驱逐，因为他不希望再就此问题进行讨论。汉考克副巡官并非不知所措，而是表现出极大的耐心，并给予他们一个多小时的时间，希望他们能和平离开。在经过一个多小时的劝说让他们离开后，他得出结论，任何进一步寻求和平解决的努力都将徒劳无功，因此他召来了防暴队。他这样做是为了尽可能避免华捕与朝鲜人之间发生任何冲突。汉考克副巡官听到华捕发表的言论，意识到种族情绪已被激起。通过召来防暴队，可以有更多外籍警察可用，从而无需使用华捕，事实正是如此，只有外籍警察参与了驱逐朝鲜人的行动。一些印度警察确实上了楼，但他们并未参与驱逐行动。
防暴队抵达后，汉考克副巡官汇报了情况

致 Furness 巡官。当时外籍警员及部分印度籍警员随后上楼进入走廊，但在最后一次要求离开被拒绝之前，并未开始驱赶朝鲜人。此时朝鲜人远非平和，其行为举止更像野蛮人而非人类。他们开始大喊大叫并挥拳相向。
任何朝鲜人都不可能被击打至昏迷，因为他们都是自行走到位于 Fairburn 总监面前的院落某处。即便在那时，他们仍在叫喊且态度十分挑衅。从事件开始到受伤朝鲜人被移交给福民医院（Foo Ming Hospital）为止，其中无人处于昏迷状态。由于走廊空间过于狭窄，不可能抓住一个人的四肢将其扔下楼。他们并非被拖拽，而是自行走到位于 Fairburn 总监面前的院落某处。他们并非被推入机动车厢，而是自行上车。一旦有交通工具可用，他们即被送往日本领事馆。抵达领事馆后，S.I. Firth 立即向日本领事馆巡查建议，任何希望前往医院的人可随即乘坐机动车厢前往。对方回复称，他们本应从戈登路直接送往医院。在记录完所有细节之前，伤者不被允许前往医院，这一过程耗时超过一小时。朝鲜人前往公共汽车公司时并非采取恳求的态度，这一点可从他们在门口强行冲破 F.S. Ball 阻拦的行为中看出；此外，Shotter 先生报告称，其中一人曾向他吐口水。

Japanese Consulate-General
Shanghai.
October 17th, 1932.

The Secretary,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Administration Building,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I have the honour to invite your attention to the
regrettable incident on September 14th between some 30 Koreans
formerly employed by the China General Omnibus Company and the
Municipal Police, the detailed report of which is enclosed
herewith. First of all, I wish to inform you that the Procurator
attached to the Japanese Court here has decided that there is no
sufficient legal grounds for prosecution of the Koreans in
question.

The Procurator is of the opinion that, as you will
see in the report attached hereto, the measures taken by the
Municipal Police in dealing with those Koreans were in excess.
In spite of their attitude of non-resistance, the Koreans were
severely beaten by the policemen. It is to be pointed out that
almost all cuts and bruises of the Koreans are found in the back
of their heads, bearing out the non-resistance on the part of the
Koreans.

Under the circumstances, I feel constrained to request
you that those members of the Municipal Police responsible for
the rough handling of the Koreans will be appropriately dealt
with.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Itaro Ishii,
Consul-General.

先生，

谨提请贵方注意9月14日发生的一起令人遗憾的事件，该事件涉及约30名前受雇于中国通用公共汽车公司的朝鲜人与市政警察，详细报告随函附上。首先，我想告知贵方，附设于此处日本法院的日本检察官已决定，对涉案朝鲜人提起诉讼缺乏充分的法律依据。

正如贵方在所附报告中看到的，检察官认为，市政警察在处理这些朝鲜人时采取的措施过当。尽管朝鲜人采取不抵抗态度，但仍遭到警察的严厉殴打。需要指出的是，几乎所有朝鲜人的割伤和挫伤都位于后脑勺，这印证了朝鲜人方面的不抵抗行为。

鉴于上述情况，我不得不请求贵方对负责粗暴对待朝鲜人的市政警察成员进行适当处理。

page_data.en:
(A) The course of events leading up to the outbreak
of the incident.

(1) The thirty-one Koreans, including Chao Yü-hsi
(趙派熙), who were employed as sub-inspectors
by the S.M.C. Gordon Road Police Station, were formerly in the
employ of the China General Trading Company, a British concern,
serving as inspectors. When some three hundred Chinese opera-
tors, who also were in the employ of the said establishment,
went on strike on August 11th, 1932, the said Korean inspectors
were notified by the Company of their dismissal for the reason
that they had neglected their duties.

It must be mentioned, in this connection, that the Koreans
claim that they had nothing to do with the strike of the Chinese
employees and resolved among themselves not to join the strike.
Yet they were dismissed simply on the pretext that they were
late in attending to their duties on that day.

Considering as they do that the measure taken by the Com-
pany was unwarrantable, the Koreans in question lost no time in
explaining to the management of the Company about the actual
circumstances of their temporary suspension of work and in sub-
mitting an appeal to the Company for their reinstatement.

Meanwhile, they conducted negotiations with the Company on
the question of their allowance, but the Company refused to
listen to their entreaties.

Thereupon, the dismissed Koreans, on September 2nd, 1932,
selected Cho Sei Ko (趙世鎬) and Sai Kei Sho (崔敬變) as
their representatives and sent them to submit to the Company a
demand comprising (1) that they should be accorded a retiring
allowance to the extent of their two years' wages per head, (2)
that expenses for their repatriation, including their passage
and train fares (second class), be granted to them and (3) that
the reserve fund which they have deposited with the Company,
five
page_data.zh:
(A) 导致事件爆发的经过。

(1) 包括赵派熙（Chao Yü-hsi）在内的三十一名朝鲜人，此前受雇于英商中国通用贸易公司（China General Trading Company）担任稽查员，后被上海公共租界工部局戈登路捕房聘为副巡官。1932年8月11日，当同样受雇于该公司的约三百名中国工人举行罢工时，该公司以这些朝鲜稽查员玩忽职守为由通知解雇他们。

在此必须提及，朝鲜人声称他们与中国员工的罢工无关，并内部决定不参加罢工。然而，他们仅以当天上班迟到为借口就被解雇。

鉴于他们认为公司采取的措施毫无道理，涉案朝鲜人随即向公司管理层解释了他们暂时停工的实际情况，并向公司提交复职申请。

与此同时，他们就津贴问题与公司进行谈判，但公司拒绝听取他们的恳求。

于是，被解雇的朝鲜人于1932年9月2日推选赵世镐（Cho Sei Ko）和崔敬变（Sai Kei Sho）为代表，向公司提交了一份要求，包括：(1) 每人给予相当于两年工资的遣散费；(2) 报销其回国费用，包括船票和火车票（二等舱/座）；(3) 退还他们存入公司的储备金，金额为

page_data.en:
- 2 -

five per cent of their wages, be refunded to them.

The two representatives, after submitting the above demand,
asked for a reply from the management of the Company.

Mr. Benner, Secretary, and Mr. Shotten, engineer-in-chief
and traffic manager, of the Company, then told the representatives
that since the Koreans were engaged locally and not sent out from
Korea, the Company had no need to meet the expenses for their
repatriation; and that the uniforms, which the Company had lent
to the Koreans, had to be returned or otherwise the Company could
not consider the matter of taking their demand into consideration.

While the negotiations between the two parties continued
thus remained unconcluded, Cho Yung Hsi (趙永熙), and two
other Koreans again visited Mr. Benner on September 6th and asked
him to give his kind consideration to the Koreans' contentions,
when he questioned the Korean representatives as to what was the
lowest estimate for the passage from Shanghai to Korea, and at the
same time told them that he would consult with the Company's
directors in order that the matter might be amicably settled.

On September 8th, Cho Yung Hsi (趙永熙) and two others,
representing the dismissed Koreans, further called at the Company's
office and held an interview with Mr. Benner.

In the course of their interview, Mr. Benner told the Koreans
that as the result of his consultation with the Company's direc-
tors, the payment of expenses for their repatriation was found
to be hopeless and that it would be advisable for the Koreans to
return their uniforms at once and to receive their wages outstan-
ding for ten days.

(2) Under the foregoing circumstances, the Company showed
no intention of complying with the demand of the Koreans. There-
fore, the dismissed, some 30 in number, with a view to effecting
a final solution of the matter, visited the Company's office on
September 12th and asked for an interview with Mr. Benner,
secretary, who however, refused to see those Koreans, requesting
them
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

其工资的百分之五。

两位代表在提交上述要求后，要求公司管理层给予答复。

公司秘书 Benner 先生和总工程师兼交通经理 Shotten 先生随后告诉代表们，由于这些朝鲜人是在本地雇佣而非从朝鲜派遣来的，公司无需承担其回国费用；并且，公司借给朝鲜人的制服必须归还，否则公司无法考虑受理他们的要求。

尽管双方谈判持续进行，但仍未得出结论，赵永熙（Cho Yung Hsi）和另外两名朝鲜人于9月6日再次拜访 Benner 先生，请他体谅朝鲜人的诉求。期间，他询问朝鲜代表从上海到朝鲜的最低船费估算是多少，同时告诉他们，他将与公司董事协商，以便友好解决此事。

9月8日，赵永熙（Cho Yung Hsi）及另外两人代表被解雇的朝鲜人再次前往公司办公室，与 Benner 先生会面。

在会谈过程中，Benner 先生告诉朝鲜人，经与公司董事协商，支付其回国费用已无希望，建议朝鲜人立即归还制服，并领取拖欠的十天工资。

(2) 鉴于上述情况，公司无意满足朝鲜人的要求。因此，为了最终解决此事，约30名被解雇者于9月12日前往公司办公室，要求会见秘书 Benner 先生，然而，Benner 先生拒绝接见这些朝鲜人，要求他们

page_data.en:
- 3 -

them to see Mr. Shotter.

The latter, at that time, happened to be out of the office,
the Koreans were told he would be returned. Nevertheless, Mr. Shotter
also refused to receive them in audience and stated that he
had so much other engagement at that time.

Mr. Cho Yung Hsi (趙永熙) and five other representatives
of the Koreans, went to see Mr. Shotter on the following day,
September 13th. The latter told the Koreans that as regards the
question of the expenses for their repatriation, he would take
it into his full consideration and would do his utmost for devis-
ing the best possible ways by consulting with the board of
directors. He questioned as to the number of members of the
Koreans' families as well as the amount of their required ex-
penses for their repatriation and then promised them that he
would give his reply in this regard on the following day, September
14th, at 3:00 p.m.

(3) Finding in Mr. Shotter's statement referred to above
a gleam of hope for the amicable settlement of the case, Cho Yung
Hsi (趙永熙) and five other representatives of the dismissed
Koreans proceeded to see Mr. Shotter at his office at 3.00 p.m.
on September 14th and asked for his reply.

He, thereupon, took the Koreans to see Mr. Benner, who, re-
ceiving them in audience, first questioned them as to their
business and then told them to the effect:-

"When I called at the Japanese Consulate this morning, I was
told that the Japanese Consular authorities would repatriate those
who have lost their jobs and cannot afford to maintain their
living, by furnishing them with expenses for repatriation.

"Why don't you take necessary procedure for your repatriation
under the protection of the Japanese Consulate-General?"

He further went on to state that when he called on the Japa-
nese Consular authorities, he told them that the demand made by
the Koreans was too much, for the Koreans estimated their passage
from
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

去见 Shotter 先生。

当时，Shotter 先生碰巧不在办公室，朝鲜人被告知他稍后会回来。尽管如此，Shotter 先生也拒绝接见他们，并表示当时他有太多其他事务缠身。

赵永熙（Cho Yung Hsi）先生及另外五名朝鲜人代表于次日，即9月13日，去见 Shotter 先生。后者告诉朝鲜人，关于回国费用的问题，他将充分考虑，并与董事会协商，尽力制定最佳方案。他询问了朝鲜人家属的人数以及所需的回国费用金额，然后承诺将于次日，即9月14日下午3点，就此给予答复。

(3) 从上述 Shotter 先生的陈述中看到案件得以友好解决的希望曙光，赵永熙（Cho Yung Hsi）及另外五名被解雇朝鲜人代表于9月14日下午3点前往 Shotter 先生的办公室寻求答复。

于是，他将朝鲜人带去见 Benner 先生，Benner 先生在接见他们时，首先询问了他们的来意，然后大致告诉他们：

“今天早上我去日本领事馆时，得知日本领事当局将为那些失业且无力维持生活的人提供回国费用，协助他们回国。

“你们为何不在日本总领事馆的保护下，办理必要的回国手续呢？”

他进一步表示，当他拜访日本领事当局时，他告诉他们，朝鲜人提出的要求太过分，因为朝鲜人估算的从

page_data.en:
- 4 -

from Shanghai to Jinsen, Korea, at $30, whereas the actual cost
was only $24, and concluded by questioning the Korean repre-
sentatives thus:-

"Is there not any other way in which you can return to
Korea with less expenses than you suggest?"

In reply, the Korean representatives told Mr. Benner as
follows:-

"The matter concerning the Japanese Consulate-General has
nothing whatever to do with our negotiations with you. It is
entirely a different question.

All of us, Koreans, have served your Company for a long
period ranging from 2 to 7 years. However, we were unceremoni-
ously compelled to retire from services against our will. We are
thus deprived of our jobs and have fallen into difficulty of
living, and yet we cannot with any grace apply to the Japanese
Consular authorities for relief. We consider that we are right
in depending upon the generosity of such a reputed Company as
yours and in looking for home after receiving reasonable amount
of retiring allowance. This is the reason why we have submitted
our entreaties to you. We firmly believe that our act in so
doing is proper and reasonable.

"It will be mentioned that $50 is what was calculated by
Mr. Shotter himself when we held our interview with him yester-
day. We have never demanded from you the above sum, but as a
matter of fact, when taken into account the passage and train
fares as well as food expenses, the sum of $50 per head is the
minimum estimate and is by no means exorbitant.

Upon hearing their explanation, both Mr. Benner and Mr.
Shotter told them that as a rule of the Company, there was no
room for the settlement of the case, unless they returned their
uniforms first. They then stated: "When we have already
been
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

从上海到朝鲜仁川（Jinsen），费用为30美元，而实际成本仅为24美元，并以如下方式质问朝鲜代表：

“难道没有其他办法能让你们以比你们所建议的更低费用返回朝鲜吗？”

对此，朝鲜代表向本纳先生（Mr. Benner）答复如下：

“关于日本总领事馆的事宜，与我们同贵公司的谈判毫无关系。这完全是另一个问题。

我们所有朝鲜人均为贵公司服务了很长一段时间，短则两年，长则七年。然而，我们在违背意愿的情况下被无礼地强制离职。因此，我们失去了工作，生活陷入困境，且我们无法体面地向日本领事当局申请救济。我们认为，依靠像贵公司这样声誉卓著的公司的慷慨，并在领取合理的遣散费后返乡，是正当的。这就是我们向你们提出恳求的原因。我们坚信，我们的行为是适当且合理的。

“有人可能会提到，50美元是昨天我们会见肖特先生（Mr. Shotter）时由他本人计算的数额。我们从未向你们索要上述金额，但事实上，考虑到船票、火车票以及伙食费，每人50美元是最低估算，绝非过高。

听到他们的解释后，本纳先生和肖特先生均告诉他们，根据公司的规定，除非他们先归还制服，否则没有解决此案的余地。随后他们表示：“既然我们已经被

prepared to return them at any moment, as soon as our demand
will have been accepted. The reason why we are still keeping
the uniforms is due to the indifferent attitude as well as to
the insincerity of the Company in its dealings with the dismis-
sed Koreans. We have no other intention than that."

Mr. Shotter is said to have stated, at this juncture,
that the uniforms being the property of the Company, they
should be returned and there would possibly be a room for recon-
sideration of the stand submitted by the Koreans.

The Korean representative, finding it necessary for them
to consult with the other Koreans on the progress of their nego-
tiations with the Company, told Mr. Shotter that they would
give their answer after consultation with their comrades and
left his office.

When they were about to get out of the Company's premises,
they met a Korean named Yo Sei Ritzu (黄成律), to whom they
asked to notify the rest of the dismissed Koreans about the
progress of the negotiations. Meanwhile, the representatives
remained at the entrance of the building, waiting for a message
to be brought from their comrades.

Upon hearing of the result of the negotiations, the Koreans
were greatly disappointed, finding a complete divergence between
the report they had received from their representatives on the
preceding day and what was notified to them at that time.

They considered that they could not afford to leave the
matter in the hands of their representatives alone.

The rest of the dismissed Koreans, 27 in number, therefore,
proceeded to the Company at about 4.15 p.m. on September 14th,
1932, and went into the building where, while remaining in the
corridor outside of Mr. Shotter's office upstairs, they caused
their six representatives to conduct further negotiations with
the

解雇，制服对我们已无用处，因此一旦我们的要求被接受，我们随时准备归还。我们之所以仍保留制服，是由于公司在对待被解雇的朝鲜人时态度冷漠且缺乏诚意。我们别无他意。”

据说肖特先生在此时表示，制服既为公司财产，理应归还，这样或许还有重新考虑朝鲜人所提立场的余地。

朝鲜代表认为有必要就与公司谈判的进展与其他朝鲜人商议，便告诉肖特先生，他们在与同伴协商后将给予答复，随即离开了他的办公室。

当他们正要离开公司办公场所时，遇到了一位名叫黄成律（Yo Sei Ritzu）的朝鲜人，他们请他通知其余被解雇的朝鲜人有关谈判的进展。与此同时，代表们留在大楼入口处，等待同伴传来的消息。

得知谈判结果后，朝鲜人大失所望，发现前一天从代表那里收到的报告与当时通知他们的情况完全不符。

他们认为不能将此事仅交由代表处理。

因此，其余27名被解雇的朝鲜人于1932年9月14日下午4点15分左右前往公司，进入大楼，在楼上肖特先生办公室外的走廊里停留，由其六名代表与公司管理层进行进一步谈判。

Mr. Shotter repeated his insistence on the return of the

(B) Circumstances which lead to the outbreak of the
incident.

The course of the negotiations conducted between the China
General Omnibus Company and the dismissed Korean inspectors has
been described as above.

The Company, while demanding from the Koreans the return
of their uniforms, requested the twenty-seven Koreans, excepting
their six representatives, to leave the Company's premises.

Meanwhile, the Koreans manifested their earnest desire to
receive a sincere, favourable reply from the Company, prior to
their return of the uniforms. While the words were being ex-
changed between the two parties, Mr. James Ball, Sergeant, No.138,
attached to the Gordon Road Station, apparently acting at the
request of the Company, placed two Chinese constables to keep
watch over the Koreans in the corridor outside Mr. Shotter's
office.

Sergeant Ball, thereupon, reported the case on telephone
to the Gordon Road Station. Upon receiving the above telephone
message, Sub-Inspector Hancock of the Gordon Road Station, ac-
companied by two foreign police officers and ten Chinese con-
stables, arrived on the scene at about 4.50 p.m. on that day
and acting in compliance with the Company's request told the
Koreans, save their six representatives, to withdraw from
the premises. But the Koreans first explained to the S.M.C.
police officers about the reason why they wished to remain there
until

the Company's management.

肖特先生再次坚持要求归还制服。他不仅拒绝了朝鲜人的恳求，还迫使除六名代表外的所有朝鲜人离开公司办公场所。

(B) 导致事件爆发的情况。

中华公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）与被解雇的朝鲜稽查员之间的谈判经过如上所述。

公司在要求朝鲜人归还制服的同时，要求除六名代表外的二十七名朝鲜人离开公司办公场所。

与此同时，朝鲜人表现出迫切希望在公司归还制服之前得到公司真诚、有利的答复。在双方交谈期间，隶属于戈登路捕房（Gordon Road Station）的138号警佐詹姆斯·鲍尔（James Ball）显然应公司要求，安排了两名华籍巡捕在肖特先生办公室外的走廊里监视朝鲜人。

随后，鲍尔警佐通过电话向戈登路捕房报告了此案。接到上述电话消息后，戈登路捕房的副督察汉考克（Hancock）陪同两名外籍警官和十名华籍巡捕，于当日下午4点50分左右抵达现场，并应公司要求，命令除六名代表外的朝鲜人离开办公场所。但朝鲜人首先向工部局警务处警官解释了为何希望留在那里，直到

until they were given a favourable reply by the Company. They
reiterated their point of view, expressing their wishes to
have the case settled amicably.

Finding himself at a loss what to do, Sub-Inspector Hancock
finally called for the dispatch of a Riot Squad.

(C) Conditions after the arrival of the Riot-Squad.

The Riot Squad, comprising about 52 members including eight
foreign officers, twelve Indian and twenty-four Chinese constables,
which was mobilized at the request of Sub-Inspector Hancock,
arrived at the premises of the Bus Company at about 7.10 p.m..

Inspector Furness, who was at that time in charge of the
Riot Squad, upon receiving a report on the situation from Sub-
Inspector Hancock, and without attempting to study the real
aspect of the condition then prevailing there, at once ordered
the eight foreign officers and ten Indian policemen to rush
upstairs of the building.

At this time, of the thirty-three Koreans, two were absent
in the water-closet and the remaining thirty-one were staying in
the corridor upstairs where a majority of them were crouching
and some standing up.

No sooner had the police force appeared upstairs than all
of its members, at a loud cry "Get out!" by one of the police
force, suddenly and almost simultaneously charged and beat the
Koreans with their batons.

In so doing, some of the policemen knocked down one of the
Koreans unconscious and kicked him down the steps of the stair-
case. Some of the policemen caught several Koreans by arms and
legs and hurled them down. By enforcing such excessive actions
the

直到得到公司的有利答复为止。他们重申了自己的观点，表达了和平解决此案的愿望。

汉考克副督察最终不知所措，于是呼叫派遣防暴队（Riot Squad）。

(C) 防暴队到达后的情况。

应汉考克副督察的要求动员的防暴队，包括八名外籍警官、十二名印籍巡捕和二十四名华籍巡捕，共约52人，于晚上7点10分左右抵达公共汽车公司办公场所。

当时负责防暴队的弗内斯督察（Inspector Furness）在听取汉考克副督察的情况报告后，未试图研究当时的真实局势，立即命令八名外籍警官和十名印籍警察冲上大楼二楼。

此时，三十三名朝鲜人中有两人在洗手间，其余三十一人留在楼上的走廊里，其中大多数人蹲着，有些人站着。

警察部队刚一出现在楼上，随着一名警察大声喊叫“出去！”，所有警员突然且几乎同时发起冲锋，并用警棍殴打朝鲜人。

在此过程中，一些警察将一名朝鲜人打昏，并将其踢下楼梯台阶。一些警察抓住几名朝鲜人的手臂和腿，将他们扔下楼。通过实施此类过度行为，警

them first to the Gordon Road Station at about 6:40 p.m. and then
to the Japanese Consulate-General at about 7:45 p.m.

(d) List of wounded Koreans and their physical conditions.

The thirty-one Koreans, who were assailed and wounded by
members of the S.M.C. Riot Squad and of the police force attached
to the Gordon Road Station, were sent to the Japanese Consulate-
General without receiving any medical treatment while they were
being held in detention at the Gordon Road Station.

Conditions of some of these wounded Koreans were found to be
of such a serious nature that they needed emergency treatment and
so the victims were at once taken to the Foo Ming Hospital in
North Szechuen Road, where they were soon attended to by Dr. Tongu,
director of the Hospital.

The following shows a list of those who were diagnosed and

(E) Remarks.

As will be seen from the above cases, nine victims require
medical treatment for a period ranging from about one month to
about three months, while the remaining six require same for a
period ranging from about three weeks to about one month.

The fact that the dismissed Koreans refused to comply with
the request by the S.M.C. police for their withdrawal from the
premises of the Omnibus Company has been testified to by the
statements of the Koreans.

However, the reason why they refused such request has to be
well understood and, it is considered, deserves careful consider-
ation. It is quite clear that the dismissed Koreans, since they
failed to receive any favourable reply from the Company in con-
nection with their entreaties, visited the offices of the Com-
pany on that day and appealed for the amicable settlement of the
outstanding matter.

When they were requested by the S.M.C. police for their
withdrawal from the Company's premises, they explained to the
police about the reason why they were staying there and solicited
the patience on the part of the police force.

The fact that these Koreans showed no disquieting or threa-
tening attitude was witnessed by Sergeant Ball and Sub-Inspector
Hancock of the Gordon Road Station, who were assigned to deal
with the Koreans. Therefore, the allegation made by the traffic
manager of the Company that the Koreans forced their way into
the Company's premises in defiance of the restraint by the police
cannot be admitted.

Superintendent Fairbairn, commander of the Riot Squad, made
a statement before the Magistrate of the Japanese Consulate-
General

(15) 李昌夏 (Li Sho Ka)，26岁，后脑遭受挫伤并有血浆渗出，需治疗约三周。

(E) 备注。

从上述案例可见，九名受害者需要接受为期约一个月至三个月的医疗救治，其余六名则需要接受为期约三周至一个月的救治。

被解雇的朝鲜人拒绝遵从工部局警务处要求其撤离公共汽车公司场地的请求，这一事实已由朝鲜人的陈述所证实。

然而，他们拒绝该请求的原因必须得到充分理解，并且被认为值得仔细考量。很明显，被解雇的朝鲜人因就其恳求事项未从公司获得任何有利答复，遂于当日前往公司办公室，呼吁友好解决悬而未决的事项。

当工部局巡捕要求其撤离公司场地时，他们向巡捕解释了滞留此处的原因，并恳请警队保持耐心。

负责处理朝鲜人事务的戈登路捕房的鲍尔（Ball）巡长和汉考克（Hancock）副巡官见证到，这些朝鲜人并未表现出令人不安或威胁性的态度。因此，该公司交通经理指控朝鲜人无视巡捕的制止强行闯入公司场地的说法不能成立。

防暴队指挥官费尔贝恩（Fairbairn）总监在日本总领事馆裁判官面前发表声明称，

page_data.en:
- 11 -

General to the effect that upon his arrival on the scene, he
received reports from Inspector Funness, Sub-Inspector Hancock,
and Mr. Shotter of the Company that "a large number of Koreans
were threatening to kill Mr. Shotter and to blow up the tank,"
(containing 3,000 gallons of gasoline, which is installed with-
in the Company's compound,) and that "they had cut off the
electrical wire in the building of the Company."

It is, however, worthy of note that no mention of this
nature was made by Mr. Shotter and Sub-Inspector Hancock them-
selves, in the course of the lengthy statements they made before
the Japanese Magistrate.

Judging from the above fact, it is easy to judge that such
false reports as described above were intentionally given to the
commander of the Riot Squad by those police officers in order
to shirk their responsibility, presumably, for fear lest the
affair should develop to assume a serious aspect.

The statement by the S.M.C. police concerned has it that
the reason why the police force charged and beat the Koreans
with batons was due to the fact that the Koreans not only refused
to obey the order for their withdrawal from the Company's pre-
mises but offered resistance by assaulting the police officers
with their fists. Therefore, the police officers concerned add,
the police suppressed the disturbance by using their batons in
lawful self-defence.

Nevertheless, the fact that there are no evidences of
members of the Riot Squad and of the Gordon Police force sus-
taining any bruises or wounds at the hands of the Koreans and
that almost all of the fifteen Korean victims sustained bruises
or wounds either in the head and/or in the back of their heads
clearly proves that the Koreans then offered no resistance and
that they had no dangerous weapons with them.

The
page_data.zh:

他抵达现场时，从芬尼斯（Funness）巡官、汉考克（Hancock）副巡官以及公司的肖特（Shotter）先生处收到报告，称“大量朝鲜人威胁要杀死肖特先生并炸毁油箱”（该油箱装有3,000加仑汽油，位于公司大院内），且“他们切断了公司大楼内的电线”。

然而，值得注意的是，肖特先生和汉考克副巡官本人在向日本裁判官所作的长篇陈述中，并未提及此类内容。

鉴于上述事实，不难判断，上述虚假报告很可能是由那些巡捕故意提供给防暴队指挥官的， presumably（大概）是出于担心事态发展成严重局面而企图推卸责任。

有关工部局巡捕的陈述称，巡捕队之所以冲锋并用警棍殴打朝鲜人，是因为朝鲜人不仅拒绝服从撤离公司场地的命令，还以拳头袭击巡捕进行抵抗。因此，有关巡捕补充道，警方使用警棍是合法的自卫行为，从而平息了骚乱。

尽管如此，防暴队和戈登路警队成员没有任何被朝鲜人造成挫伤或伤口的事实，以及十五名朝鲜受害者中几乎所有人都在头部和/或后脑遭受挫伤或伤口的事实，清楚地证明朝鲜人当时并未进行抵抗，且身上没有携带危险武器。

page_data.en:
- 12 -

The last mentioned fact, in particular, convincingly shows
that from the very beginning, they had no intention whatsoever
of doing any harm to any outsiders or of creating a disturbance,
their only and sole object being to obtain a favourable reply
from the management of the Company.

It must be mentioned, therefore, that while the Koreans,
though they simply refused to retire from the Company's premises,
were remaining calm, showing no disquieting attitude, the Riot
Squad was called out with the consequence that many Koreans were
assaulted and wounded.

In such circumstance, it seems that the police who have
inflicted such serious injuries upon the defenceless Koreans,
and whose duty, needless to say, is to give protection to lives
and property of the public, have over-ridden their commission and
that their action constitutes an abuse of their official
authority.

Finally, as regards the charges under which the thirty-one
Koreans have been prosecuted by the S.M.C. Police Force, it must
be mentioned that as already stated, Cho Yung Hsi (趙永熙)
and five other Koreans, presented themselves in the Company's
office as the representatives of the dismissed Koreans and in
accordance with the suggestion made by the management of the
Company on the preceding day, September 13th, and therefore
their presence within the premises is by no means unlawful and
does not constitute any crime.

As for the remaining twenty-five Koreans, it will be recalled
that they repaired to the Company one after another in a peaceful
manner, and that close investigations made by the Japanese police
authorities reveal that there are no evidences of these Koreans
either unlawfully trespassing on the Company's premises or
breaking
page_data.zh:
- 12 -

特别是最后提到的事实，令人信服地表明，从一开始他们就毫无伤害任何外人或制造骚乱的意图，他们唯一且单纯的目的就是从公司管理层那里获得有利的答复。

因此必须指出，虽然朝鲜人仅仅只是拒绝离开公司场地，并保持冷静，未表现出令人不安的态度，但防暴队仍被出动，导致许多朝鲜人遭到袭击并受伤。

在这种情况下，对毫无防备的朝鲜人造成如此严重伤害的巡捕——其职责不言而喻是保护公众的生命和财产——似乎越权行事，其行为构成了滥用职权。

最后，关于工部局警务处起诉三十一名朝鲜人所依据的指控，必须指出，如前所述，赵永熙（Cho Yung Hsi）和其他五名朝鲜人作为被解雇朝鲜人的代表出现在公司办公室，这是按照公司管理层在前一天（9月13日）提出的建议行事的，因此他们在场地内的出现绝非非法，也不构成任何犯罪。

至于其余二十五名朝鲜人，回顾可知，他们是相继以和平方式前往公司的，且日本警方当局进行的深入调查显示，没有证据表明这些朝鲜人非法侵入公司场地或破坏

page_data.en:
- 13 -

breaking the public peace. It is true that they visited the
Company at their own free will without any previous arrangements
with the management of the Company and also it is true that they
did not comply with the request by the Company's representative
as well as by the members of the S.M.J. Police force. But the
above fact is not to be taken as constituting an offence against
which the Koreans deserve to be prosecuted.
Furthermore, the manner in which all the Koreans in question
behaved while remaining within the premises cannot be construed
as an act of interference of any members of the S.M.P. Police
Force in exercising their public duties.

------------------
page_data.zh:
- 13 -

破坏公共安宁。诚然，他们是自愿前往公司，此前未与公司管理层做任何安排；同样诚然的是，他们并未遵从公司代表以及工部局警务处（S.M.J. Police force，原文如此，应为S.M.P.）成员的要求。但上述事实不应被视为构成应对朝鲜人提起诉讼的罪行。
此外，所有相关朝鲜人在滞留场地期间的行为方式，不能被解释为干扰工部局警务处（S.M.P. Police Force）任何成员执行公务的行为。

Sixteen ex-Korean Inspectors of the China General
Omnibus Company, who were recently dismissed from this concern,
together with their families and 19 other destitute Koreans,

November 18, 1932. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

MAINICHI

JAPANESE ARRESTED BY JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

At 11.35 a.m. November 17 the
Shanghai Japanese Consular Police received a telegram
from the Osaka Police requesting the arrest of a Japanese
named G. Yoshihara, 29, staying in the Katsuta Hotel
on Seward Road on a charge of misappropriation.
Sub-Inspector Yamasaki of the
Consular Police proceeded to the hotel but found that
the man had already removed to No. 438 Dixwell Road.
At about 3 p.m. the Sub-Inspector arrested the wanted
man at the latter address. The prisoner has admitted
the misappropriation of Yen 1,500.00 belonging to his
employer.

JAPANESE CONSUL-GENERAL CALLS ON CHIEF OF PUBLIC
SAFETY BUREAU

At 3 p.m. November 17 Mr. Ishii,
Japanese Consul-General, called on Mr. Wen, Chief of
the Public Safety Bureau to return the visit Mr. Wen
had made.

MAINICHI

FORMER KOREAN INSPECTORS OF BUS COMPANY LEAVE FOR
MANCHURIA

The Korean Inspectors who were
discharged from the Bus Company together with their
families will leave Shanghai for Manchuria to-day on
the S.S. Hoten Maru. The Japanese Consulate is paying
their fares.

NICHI-NICHI

CHINESE PLAY JOKES ON JAPANESE GIRL STUDENTS

Of late several instances of
Chinese playing jokes on Japanese girl students have
been reported.
On November 12 Chinese coolies
in the vicinity of Carter Road played jokes on 5 Japanese
Girls' School students.
It is to be hoped that the
Shanghai Municipal Police will put a stop to this.

Translation of a French Police Report dated 6.10.32.

139/2

ACTIVITY OF KOREAN COMMUNISTS IN THE FRENCH CONCESSION

The Korean Communist Party works, in China, in close contact with the Chinese Communist Party. In Shanghai, the Korean Communists form a special branch of the local committee of the Chinese Communist Party. The Committee of the Korean Branch, as well as all the Korean Communist Cells used to be installed in the French Concession, where the majority of the Koreans reside. The principal role played by Korean Communists residing in China follows instructions issued by the Komintern:-

1. To spread propaganda among their nationals.
2. To struggle against nationalist tendencies in the midst of Korean emigrants.
3. To struggle against the "imperialists".

In this connection, the Korean Communists are forming a special section under the wing of the "League against Imperialism and for Colonial Independence" (an auxiliary organization of the III Internationale)- and are closely working with the other Eastern sections of this League, such as:-

Indo-Chinese, Philippine, Formosan Sections etc.etc.

The danger of this work is evident, because, notably the Korean elements have taken a very active part in the work of the pseudo-committee of Foreign revolutionary soldiers stationed in Shanghai, many members of which were arrested at the commencement of June 1931. This committee is engaged in spreading communist propaganda among the various foreign troops stationed in Shanghai. The Korean members were especially charged with the spreading of propaganda among English, American and Japanese troops. It is

1932年10月6日法国警方报告的译文。

139/2

法租界内朝鲜共产党人的活动

朝鲜共产党在中国与中国共产党保持密切联系。在上海，朝鲜共产党人组成中国共产党地方委员会的一个特别支部。朝鲜支部委员会以及所有朝鲜共产党小组过去都设在法租界，因为大多数朝鲜人居住在那里。居住在中国的朝鲜共产党人所扮演的主要角色，是遵循共产国际发出的指示：-

1. 在本国国民中开展宣传。
2. 在朝鲜移民中反对民族主义倾向。
3. 反对“帝国主义者”。

为此，朝鲜共产党人正在“反帝同盟及争取殖民地独立联盟”（第三国际的附属组织）的庇护下组建一个特别部门，并与该联盟的其他东方部门密切合作，例如：-

印度支那、菲律宾、台湾等部门等等。

这项工作的危险性是显而易见的，特别是朝鲜分子积极参与了设在上海的外国革命士兵伪委员会的工作，该委员会许多成员于1931年6月初被捕。该委员会致力于向驻扎在上海的各外国军队传播共产主义宣传。朝鲜成员尤其负责在英国、美国和日本军队中传播宣传。值得注意的是

page_data.en:
-2-
interesting to note that this Committee receives
from the Department of Agitation and propaganda of
the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party
all the literature which was to be distributed among
the foreign troops. These tracts were received in
the Chinese language, and the different sections of
"The Committee of Foreign revolutionary soldiers"
translate them into French, English, Japanese, etc.
It is to be particularly noted that whilst the
Annamite Section of the said committee is located in
the International Settlement, the Head Offices of the
Korean Branch are to be found in the French Concession.
After the arrest of several members of the Committee
in question, the work of spreading propaganda among
the foreign soldiers, was confided by the Central
Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, in the
different Chinese and Korean cells. The Korean cells
in particular were charged with the spreading of
propaganda in the French Concession, a statement which
is proved by the declarations of the Korean Communist
Num Long Sup, Secretary of the 1st cell of the local
Korean Branch of the Chinese Communist Party. This
person was arrested on October 3, 1932, by our
Political Branch at the request of the Japanese
Authorities. According to Num, the cell that he used to
be in charge of, had to distribute communist tracts,
in French and in Quoc-Nu, in front of the barracks of
the French troops.
Finally, the activities of the Korean Communist
Party are as dangerous as those of the Chinese Communist
Party, under whose orders it functions in Shanghai.
Attached herewith is a copy of the statement of
Num Lan Sup.
page_data.zh:
-2-
该委员会从中国共产党中央委员会的宣传鼓动部接收所有拟分发给外国军队的文献。这些传单以中文接收，由“外国革命士兵委员会”的各个部门将其翻译成法语、英语、日语等。特别值得注意的是，虽然该委员会的安南（越南）部门位于公共租界，但朝鲜支部的总部却设在法租界。在该委员会几名成员被捕后，向外国士兵传播宣传的工作由中国共产党中央委员会委托给各个中国和朝鲜小组。特别是朝鲜小组被责成在法租界传播宣传，这一说法得到了朝鲜共产党人Num Long Sup（音译）声明的证实，他是中国共产党地方朝鲜支部第一小组的秘书。此人于1932年10月3日应日本当局要求，被我政治处逮捕。据Num称，他负责的小组必须在法国军营前分发用法语和国语（Quoc-Nu，即越南语）书写的共产主义传单。
最后，朝鲜共产党的活动与中国共产党的活动一样危险，它在上海是在中国共产党的命令下行事的。
随函附上Num Lan Sup（音译）的声明副本。

page_data.en:
A. PARK □UL □HAT (          ).
Q. Do you know PARK personally ?
A. Yes.
Q. Where is he now ?
A. On October 28 he was arrested in Koukaza Park.
Q. Has PARK any distinctive marks by which he could be easily
identified ?
A. Yes! The top of the joints of the fingers on his right hand are
missing.
Q. What was PARK's part in the Korean Communist Movement ?
A. He was the leader of the Korean branch of the Chinese Communist
Party in Shanghai.
Q. What part did you play ?
A. I was in charge of a cell.
Q. How many cells are there in Shanghai ?
A. Only two.
Q. How many members are there in your cell ?
A. Five.
Q. Who were the members of your cell ?
A. KIM DAL SAN, OH TAI YUN, PARK CHUN SHAN, KIM HUNG LUI.
Q. Did you meet often ?
A. Once a week/
Q. Where ?
A. Sometimes in my house, sometimes in the Koukaza Park, sometimes in
teashops in the French Concession.
Q. Do you know the Head of the second cell ?
A. Yes ! KIM SHUNG LAI.
Q. What type of work was your cell doing ?
A. Propaganda work; I used to receive propaganda literature from
PARK CHUN SHAN which I in turn gave to the members of the cell;
it was their job to distribute it among sympathetic Korean residents.
Further we had to spread propaganda among the Japanese soldiers.
Q. Were you in liaison with the Chinese Communist Party ?
A. No, not directly, this liaison being effected by the intermediary of
PARK CHUN SHAN.
page_data.zh:
A. PARK □UL □HAT (          )。
问：你个人认识PARK吗？
答：认识。
问：他现在在哪里？
答：10月28日他在虹口公园被捕。
问：PARK有什么易于识别的显著特征吗？
答：有！他右手手指关节顶部缺失。
问：PARK在朝鲜共产主义运动中扮演什么角色？
答：他是中国共产党上海朝鲜支部的领导人。
问：你扮演什么角色？
答：我负责一个小组。
问：上海有多少个小组？
答：只有两个。
问：你的小组有多少成员？
答：五名。
问：你的小组成员是谁？
答：KIM DAL SAN, OH TAI YUN, PARK CHUN SHAN, KIM HUNG LUI。
问：你们经常见面吗？
答：每周一次。
问：在哪里？
答：有时在我家，有时在虹口公园，有时在法租界的茶馆里。
问：你认识第二小组的负责人吗？
答：认识！KIM SHUNG LAI。
问：你的小组从事什么类型的工作？
答：宣传工作；我从PARK CHUN SHAN那里接收宣传文献，然后转交给小组成员；他们的任务是将这些文献分发给持同情态度的朝鲜居民。此外，我们还必须在日本士兵中传播宣传。
问：你与中国共产党有联系吗？
答：没有直接联系，这种联系是通过PARK CHUN SHAN作为中介进行的。

page_data.en:
Q. Do you know the names of influential members of the Chinese
Communist Party ?
A. No.
Q. Were you in liaison with foreign communists ?
A. No.
Q. Do you receive any money for your work ?
A. No.
Q. Who printed the literature for the communist propaganda ?
A. Korean literature was printed at 637 Rue Ratard with a
duplicator. I do not know where the Chinese and Japanese
literature was printed.
Q. Do you know where the literature, written in English and French,
found at your house, was printed ?
A. No. This literature was given to me about three weeks ago by
PARK CHUN HAN.
Q. How many copies did you receive ?
A. About 60 ...30 in English and 30 in French.
Q. What have you done with this literature ?
A. The members of my cell, acting on instructions from PARK CHUN HAN,
had it distributed in front of the barracks of the French
soldiers. The English literature was distributed by Cell No. 2.
Q. What languages can you speak ?
A. Korean, Japanese and a little Shanghai dialect.
page_data.zh:
问：你知道中国共产党有影响力的成员的名字吗？
答：不知道。
问：你与外国共产党人有联系吗？
答：没有。
问：你的工作有报酬吗？
答：没有。
问：共产主义宣传文献是在哪里印刷的？
答：朝鲜文文献是在拉都路637号用油印机印刷的。我不知道中文和日文文献是在哪里印刷的。
问：你知道在你家中发现的英文和法文文献是在哪里印刷的吗？
答：不知道。这些文献是大约三周前由PARK CHUN HAN交给我的。
问：你收到了多少份？
答：大约60份……30份英文和30份法文。
问：你是如何处理这些文献的？
答：我小组的成员按照PARK CHUN HAN的指示，将其分发在法国士兵的营房前。英文文献由第二小组分发。
问：你会说哪些语言？
答：朝鲜语、日语和一点上海话。

Six Korean Communists arrested in French Concession.

On October 3, our Political Branch made raids on
the following addresses :-
637 Rue Ratard, where an important quantity of
Communist literature in Chinese, Korean and several foreign
languages was seized and the following three Koreans
arrested :-
Chung Il Pyeng or Zie Y Bing (錢 平), aged 27.

At 622 Rue Bourgeat where several letters and photo-

At about 12.30 p.m. on September 28 members of our
political section arrested at the request of the Japanese
Consular Authorities in the Koukaza Garden, one named Cho
Pong An (Korean pronunciation) or Chao Feng Yen (曹奉岩)

It will be recalled that one Cho Pong An was already
mentioned on several occasions in our previous reports.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 17, 1932

STRONG ARM METHODS
PROTESTED
Japanese Authorities To
Probe Charges Of
Undue Force

Pending the completion of inquiries into the circumstances leading up to the arrest and detention of the several Korean ex-employees of the China General Omnibus Company and the dispatch to hospital of others who came into collision with the Settlement police, no statement is to be made upon the occurrence by local Japanese authorities, it was learned yesterday.

The charge of unnecessary force levelled against members of the S. M. P. Riot Squad who were summoned to quell the disturbance is one of the matters to be investigated further, a Japanese official explained when approached upon the subject yesterday.

It has been claimed in certain quarters that the police used more force than necessary in their suppression of the outbreak and the Japanese authorities are inquiring to discover if such was the case. More than half a dozen of the rioters had to be treated in hospital for scalp wounds alleged to have been inflicted by police batons.

September 16, 1932. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

AICHI

NEWLY APPOINTED CHIEF OF 5TH DIVISION
PUBLIC SAFETY BUREAU ASSURES PROTECTION TO
JAPANESE

At 11.30 a.m. September 15,
Mr. Ching Koo, who was recently appointed Chief
of the 5th Division of the Public Safety Bureau,
called on Mr. Hanasato, Chief of the Japanese
Consular Police Station, at the Japanese Consulate
to announce his appointment.
He then made the following
statement to reporters who were present:-
"Should any trouble occur
between the Japanese and the Chinese, I will deal
with it, pursuing a policy of justice. I will
afford adequate protection to the lives of the
Japanese and their property. You are requested to
keep me informed on all matters that do not come
under the authority of the Police. The members
of the Peace Maintenance Corps are out on duty to-day
(September 15) as a precautionary measure against
the Communists' plan to create disturbances. Should
any of the Japanese observing the activities of the
Public Safety Bureau spread rumours that fighting
has commenced between Japan and China, you are
requested to inform them that the report is incorrect.
The Communist Party has declared that it will make
assaults on Japanese between September 15 and 18
and will attack the Municipality of Greater Shanghai,
and the Stations of the Public Safety Bureau. I am
of the opinion that it will not be carried out but
end simply in an empty threat and propaganda.
Nevertheless, the Peace Maintenance Corps has been
mobilized to be prepared for any untoward incidents."

MISCELLANEOUS

on 14 persons and adopting an outrageous attitude
towards the Koreans as if they were dealing with
animals. It is evident from the nature of the
wounds that the Koreans put up no opposition to the
Police. The victims visited the Bus Company's offices
to negotiate with the management and to appeal
against their unlawful dismissal. The Police, who
were adequately armed and outnumbered the Koreans,
surrounded and assaulted the latter to their heart's
content. The attitude of the Shanghai Municipal
Police towards the Japanese has recently become
objectionable. This has been clearly shown on the
occasion of the Nanking Road and Bus Company Incidents.
There is no doubt that the Shanghai Municipal Police,
whose duty is to protect the public, are resorting to
tyranny and oppression. Should the Shanghai Municipal
Police continue to pursue such an oppressive form of
administration, it is feared what the outcome of the
next affair might be.

MAINICHI

STATEMENT BY MR. HANASATO, CHIEF OF
JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE STATION

Mr. Hanasato, Chief of the
Japanese Consular Police Station, made the following
statement to a reporter on September 15:-
"According to the Koreans' version,
they offered no resistance to the Police. This is
corroborated in today's (September 15) Chinese and
foreign newspapers. The fault on the part of the
Koreans was that they did not obey the order of the
Police and disperse. Notwithstanding, it is unlawful
on the part of the Police to immediately resort to
violence because their order was refused. To adopt
direct action against our nationals may be regarded
as an excess of duty by the Police. Our Consular
Police should be immediately informed when Police
order are disobeyed. Then our officers will proceed
to the scene. If the order is again disobeyed, then
the offenders will be arrested and dealt with
according to law. Regarding the incident in question,
I would like to have been informed in time. Had I
been informed, the incident might have been avoided.
Up to the present I have only heard the statement of
the victims. I am awaiting statements from the Police
and the Bus management and will then adopt appropriate
measure to deal with the case."

对14人施暴，并对朝鲜人采取蛮横态度，仿佛对待牲畜一般。从伤口性质来看，显然朝鲜人并未对警察进行任何抵抗。受害者前往公共汽车公司办事处，旨在与管理层谈判，并就其非法解雇提出申诉。警方武装充足，人数多于朝鲜人，却将后者包围并肆意殴打。上海公共租界工部局警务处近期对日本人的态度已引起反感。南京路事件及公共汽车公司事件已清楚地表明了这一点。毫无疑问，负有保护公众职责的上海公共租界工部局警务处正在诉诸暴政与压迫。若上海公共租界工部局警务处继续推行此种压迫性管理方式，恐难预料下一事件之结局。

《每日新闻》

日本领事馆警察署署长花里（Hanasato）先生的声明

日本领事馆警察署署长花里先生于9月15日向一名记者发表如下声明：
“据朝鲜人方面称，他们未对警察进行抵抗。今日（9月15日）的中外报纸均证实了这一点。朝鲜人的过错在于未服从警察命令解散。尽管如此，警察仅因命令被拒便立即诉诸暴力，实属违法。对我国国民采取直接行动，可被视为警察越权行为。当警察命令遭到违抗时，应立即通知我方领事馆警察。届时我方警官将赶赴现场。若命令再次遭到违抗，则违法者将被逮捕并依法处置。关于本案，我本希望能及时获知消息。若我早得通知，此事或许可以避免。截至目前，我仅听取了受害者的陈述。我正等待警方及公共汽车管理方的陈述，随后将采取适当措施处理此案。”

MISCELLANEOUS

ASAHINICHI, NICHINICHI AND NIPPO

THE BUS COMPANY INCIDENT

The Shanghai Municipal Police
are adversely criticized for having abused their
authority in the case of assault on the dismissed
Korean inspectors of the General Omnibus Company.
Sympathies are being extended to the injured Koreans.
At 1 p.m. September 16, the
Standing Committee of the Japanese Amalgamated
Association of Street Unions will hold an emergency
meeting to discuss the assault case in order to
impeach the unlawful action of the Police.
The Japanese public are also
advocating that a mass meeting be held for the
purpose of accusing the Shanghai Municipal Police
for their abuse of authority.

Charge of Inciting to Riot may not
be materialized

Between 10 a.m. and noon
September 15, the hearing of the case, in which
31 Koreans were charged by the Shanghai Municipal
Police with the offence of disturbing the peace,
trespassing and assaulting Police Officers, was
held at the Japanese Consulate.
It is believed that the charge
of inciting to riot brought against the Koreans
will not be materialized for the following reasons:-
"The Korean inspectors were
invited to be present at the Bus Company's offices
on the day in question and they did not go there
with the object of creating a disturbance. They
did not adopt any threatening attitude towards the
Bus management and did not oppose the Police when
the latter entered the premises. The only charge
against them is that they did not obey the order
of the Police to disperse, which they refused,
declaring that they would wait for the Company's
reply on the matter which had been promised to them
by the manager. No justifiable reason exists to
support the action adopted by the Police."

公共汽车公司事件

上海公共租界工部局警务处因在殴打通用公共汽车公司被解雇的朝鲜籍查票员一案中滥用职权而受到严厉批评。人们正对受伤的朝鲜人表示同情。
9月16日下午1时，日本街道工会联合会常务委员会将举行紧急会议，讨论该殴打案，以谴责警方的非法行为。
日本公众也主张召开群众大会，指控上海公共租界工部局警务处滥用职权。

煽动暴乱罪指控可能无法成立

9月15日上午10时至中午，日本领事馆审理了上海公共租界工部局警务处指控31名朝鲜人犯有扰乱治安、非法侵入及袭击警官罪行的案件。
据信，针对朝鲜人提出的煽动暴乱罪指控将不会成立，理由如下：
“当日，朝鲜籍查票员是受邀前往公共汽车公司办事处的，他们去那里并非为了制造骚乱。他们未对公共汽车管理层采取任何威胁性态度，且在警察进入办公场所时也未进行抵抗。对他们的唯一指控是不服从警察解散的命令，他们拒绝解散，声称要等待经理曾答应给予的公司答复。警方的行动缺乏正当理由支持。”

攻击性态度。上海公共租界工部局警务处也承认，朝鲜人未采取任何威胁性态度，且未见动荡迹象。

MISCELLANEOUS

JINICHI, NICHI'ICHI AND NIPPO

CRAZY S.M.P. OFFICERS COMMIT VIOLENCE
ON KOREANS: BLOODY TRAGEDY IN FRONT OF
BUS COMPANY'S OFFICES

The Shanghai ... Nichinichi
publishes the following report under the above
heading:-
At 7.40 p.m. September 14, the
Japanese Consular Police received a telephone message
from the Gordon Road Police Station stating that
some 30 Korean ex-inspectors of the Bus Company, who
were recently dismissed, had been arrested for
creating a disturbance in front of the Company
premises on Connaught Road and that they were being
sent to the Consulate. Shortly afterwards,
the Koreans arrived in trucks and were handed
over to the Consular Police.
Inquiries show the following
circumstances to be responsible for the trouble:-
"On September 13, a notice was
received requesting that representatives of the
dismissed Korean inspectors be present at the Company
at 3 p.m. September 14. Six representatives presented
themselves and 25 Koreans later visited the place
to ascertain the result of the meeting. They were
ordered by the foreign and Chinese Police Officers
to disperse. After a struggle, just as the inspectors
were about to enter a room on the 1st floor of the
Company's offices, a party of Police Officers arrived
in the red van and, without making enquiries into
the circumstances of the case, ruthlessly assaulted
the Koreans with their truncheons."
Injuries were inflicted on 14
Koreans, 8 of whom were so seriously injured that
they were detained at the Foo Ling Hospital. Sai
Yei Ki and other four persons are reported to be in
a critical condition.

Statement of Mr. Hanasato, Chief of Japanese
Consular Police Station

Mr. Hanasato, Chief of the
Japanese Consular Police Station, made the following
statement to reporters who visited him at the
Consulate yesterday:-
"I can state nothing definite
about the incident because detailed investigations have
not yet been made. It is a matter for regret that
such violence has been committed on persons who had
no intention to resist the Police nor were capable

疯狂的工部局警务处官员对朝鲜人施暴：公共汽车公司办事处前的血腥悲剧

上海……《日日新闻》以上述标题刊登了以下报道：
9月14日晚7时40分，日本领事馆警察接到戈登路警站的电话通知，称约30名近期被解雇的公共汽车公司朝鲜籍前查票员因在康纳路（Connaught Road）公司 premises 前制造骚乱而被捕，并将被送往领事馆。不久后，朝鲜人被卡车运抵并移交给领事馆警察。
经查询，导致此次纠纷的情况如下：
“9月13日，收到通知要求被解雇的朝鲜籍查票员代表于9月14日下午3时到公司。六名代表到场，随后又有25名朝鲜人前往该地以了解会议结果。中外籍警官命令他们解散。在一番争执后，正当查票员们准备进入公司办事处一楼的一个房间时，一群警官乘坐红色面包车抵达，在未调查案件具体情况的情况下，用警棍残酷殴打朝鲜人。”
14名朝鲜人受伤，其中8人伤势严重，被留治于福林医院（Foo Ling Hospital）。据报道，Sai Yei Ki（音译）及其他四人情况危急。

日本领事馆警察署署长花里先生的声明

日本领事馆警察署署长花里先生昨日在领事馆向来访记者发表如下声明：
“由于尚未进行详细调查，我无法就该事件作出确切说明。令人遗憾的是，对既无意抵抗警察也无能力抵抗的人施加了如此暴力。例如，当朝鲜人

page_data.en:

MISCELLANEOUS

of doing so. For instance, when the Koreans
refused to obey the order of the Police, it was
not necessary, in my opinion, that the latter should
have resorted to violence particularly in view of
the fact that there exists a Japanese Police Station
here. To commit violence on foreigners by the Police
is undesirable in view of the present situation. I
hope the Police will exercise a little more care."

The Japanese Consular Authorities
regard the incident as grave. It is reported that
a strong protest will be lodged with the
Shanghai Municipal Council. The issue of the case
is being watched carefully.

JINICHI, NICHINICHI AND NIPLC

FIRE-CRACKERS THROWN INTO JAPANESE SHOP

At 6 p.m., September 14, when
a number of Chinese customers were selecting piece
goods at the Shisaki Service Department, No. 43
West Kashing Road, a Chinese youth, aged 20, appeared
from the direction of Woosung Road and threw a
large fire-cracker into the premises. Two Chinese
received burns on the legs caused by the explosion.
Officers of the Consular Police
and the Hongkew Station immediately arrived on the
scene but the offender had already escaped.
Students of the Chinese school
on the opposite side of the shop frequently threaten
Chinese who purchase goods at the shop and also
throw stones into the premises. It is considered
that the present case might be a mischievous act
by students of the school.

拒绝服从警察命令时，我认为警方没有必要诉诸暴力，特别是考虑到此处设有日本警察署。鉴于当前局势，警察对外国人施暴是不可取的。我希望警方能更加谨慎。”

日本领事当局视此事件为严重事件。据报道，将向上海公共租界工部局提出强烈抗议。人们正密切关注此案的结果。

《字林西报》、《日日新闻》及《日本新闻报》

鞭炮被扔进日本商店

9月14日下午6时，当数名中国顾客在西嘉善路43号四崎服务社（Shisaki Service Department）挑选布匹时，一名20岁的中国青年从吴淞路方向出现，并向店内投掷了一枚大型鞭炮。爆炸导致两名中国人腿部烧伤。
领事馆警察和虹口警站的警官立即赶到现场，但肇事者已逃脱。
商店对面中国学校的学生经常威胁在该店购物的中国人，并向店内投掷石块。认为本案可能是该校学生的恶作剧。

1932年9月1日下午4时15分，收到在中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）执勤的 O.P.C. 244 的电话留言，报告管理层在与数名朝鲜籍前督察发生纠纷。在警长汉考克（Hancock）和弗斯（Firth）的带领下，一队警察前往现场。总工程师兼经理 J.D.K. Shotton 先生接受了问询，他请求警方将这些朝鲜人驱逐出公共汽车公司的场所，因为双方无法达成协议。这些聚集在 Shotton 先生办公室外的朝鲜籍前督察总人数约为30人，警方随后要求并劝告他们和平离开该场所。他们反复表示希望 Shotton 先生回答更多问题，而警方也反复劝告他们离开该场所。下午5时，他们最终被告知

REPORT
Date Sept. 17 / 1932
Subject (in full) Meeting of Standing Committee of Association of Japanese
Street Unions.
Made by D.C. Imamura. Forwarded by Tho Robertson, Supt.

Between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. September 16, a special
meeting of the Standing Committee of the Local Japanese
Amalgamated Association of Street Unions, was held in the
Japanese Club on Boone Road when it was resolved to make the
following demands to the S.M.C. through the Consul General for
Japan :-
1. Police officers who assaulted Koreans are to be dismissed.
2. Officer i/c Gordon Road Station is to be severely punished.
3. All officers concerned are to be punished.
4. Koreans are to receive reasonable indemnity for injuries
from S.M.C. Authorities.
In the event of these demands being rejected by the
S.M.C. a general meeting of Japanese residents will be held,
and necessary steps will be taken.
At 10 a.m. September 17, Mr. Y. Hayashi, chairman of the
above association will have a meeting with Mr. Bell, chairman of
S.M.C. to seek his opinion on the above four points.
He will also call on the Commander of the Japanese
Naval 3rd Fleet to ascertain the progress made in the negotiations
with the S.M.C. in the matter of the Nanking Road incident of
September 2.

C.P.

报告
日期：1932年9月17日
主题（全称）：日本街道工会联合会常务委员会会议。
制作人：今村（Imamura）副巡官。由 superintendent 罗伯逊（Tho Robertson）转发。

9月16日下午3时至4时之间，本地日本街道工会联合会在布恩路（Boone Road）的日本俱乐部举行了常务委员会特别会议，会上决议通过日本总领事向工部局提出以下要求：
1. 殴打朝鲜人的警察须予撤职。
2. 戈登路（Gordon Road）巡捕房负责人须受严厉惩处。
3. 所有涉事警察须受惩处。
4. 工部局当局须对朝鲜人所受伤害给予合理赔偿。
如果工部局拒绝这些要求，将举行日本居民大会，并采取必要步骤。
9月17日上午10时，上述协会主席林（Y. Hayashi）先生将与工部局主席贝尔（Bell）先生会晤，就上述四点征求其意见。
他还将拜访日本海军第三舰队司令，以了解关于9月2日南京路事件与工部局谈判的进展。

C.P.
